💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A soli 16 anni esordiva in Serie A, sul suo talento si era fatto avanti anche il Bayern Monaco, poi ha trovato la sua strada a Bologna e aspetta un giorno di tornare in Italia.
  • Industry observers note that come sta andando l'esperienza?
  • Ha debuttato in Serie A a 16 anni con il Chievo.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A soli 16 anni esordiva in Serie A, sul suo talento si era fatto avanti anche il Bayern Monaco, poi ha trovato la sua strada a Bologna e aspetta un giorno di tornare in Italia. Emanuel Vignato, esterno offensivo che ha fatto molto parlare di sé in passato, oggi gioca al Forte Virtus di Dubai e in esclusiva con Tuttomercatoweb.com analizza tutti i temi che hanno scandito la sua carriera. A partire dalla scelta di approdare negli Emirati: "È nata con l'idea di voler cambiare un po' aria. Avevo anche qualche possibilità in Italia, però poi ho scelto e ho preferito provare a cambiare. Vedremo se avrò avuto ragione o meno".

Industry observers note that come sta andando l'esperienza? "I primi mesi sono stati difficili, un po' per il caldo e per il clima. Ci alleniamo quasi sempre la mattina presto, però si arrivava a fare 37-38 gradi e all'inizio non ero abituato. Gli allenamenti sono abbastanza intensi e il caldo non aiutava di sicuro, soprattutto rispetto agli altri ragazzi, che erano già abituati a queste condizioni. Adesso, però, già da qualche settimana sto meglio e anche il clima si è un po' raffreddato".

Ha debuttato in Serie A a 16 anni con il Chievo. Che ricordi ha di Verona? "Il Chievo è stata un'esperienza bellissima, perché è il posto in cui sono cresciuto. Fin da bambino ho sempre giocato lì, mi hanno fatto esordire e sono riuscito a trascorrere anche qualche anno in prima squadra. Credo di avere i ricordi più belli legati al Chievo, anche perché abitavo a Verona, la mia città, ed ero a casa con la famiglia e gli amici".

Il ricordo dell'esordio in Serie A, arrivato quando era ancora minorenne, è ancora tangibile nella sua mente? "L'esordio è, credo per tutti, uno dei momenti più belli della carriera. È la prima volta in cui giochi in un campionato così importante, un momento che hai sempre sognato. Direi che è sicuramente uno dei ricordi più belli che ho".

Industry observers note that negli anni del suo esordio col Chievo si parlava molto di un interesse del Bayern Monaco nei suoi confronti. C'è stato qualcosa di concreto? "C'è stato un periodo in cui erano venuti a parlare direttamente con noi in famiglia, insieme al procuratore che avevo in quel momento. Poi, in realtà, non so bene come siano andati i discorsi con il Chievo, perché dovevano mettersi d'accordo tra loro. Io avevo il contratto in scadenza, mi restava soltanto un anno, quindi avrebbero dovuto trovare un'intesa. Ero in ritiro con il Chievo, ricordo ancora quello estivo, e poi mi hanno detto che in qualche modo non si era trovato un accordo. Alla fine sono rimasto al Chievo".

Dopo l'esperienza a Verona è arrivata quella con il Bologna, che è stata piuttosto lunga. "Anche di Bologna ho dei bellissimi ricordi. È stata la mia prima esperienza fuori casa, perché avevo sempre giocato al Chievo. È stato un po' strano dover andare via a un certo punto, però conservo ricordi bellissimi della città, della squadra, di tutti gli allenatori che ho avuto e dei tifosi. È probabilmente la squadra in cui mi sono trovato meglio".

Industry observers note that tra gli allenatori che ha avuto in quel periodo c'è stato Sinisa Mihajlovic, che oggi non è più con noi. Che impatto ha avuto sul suo percorso? "Credo che in quegli anni mi abbia aiutato tantissimo. Sono arrivato abbastanza giovane e, anche se venivo già da qualche anno di esperienza, lì c'erano giocatori con molta più esperienza di me. Con i suoi consigli mi ha aiutato ad ambientarmi e poi mi ha fatto giocare abbastanza. Sicuramente ho bei ricordi di lui".

Ce n’è uno in particolare? "Mi diceva sempre di giocare come sapevo, senza avere paura, e di provare a fare sempre qualcosa in più. Mi ripeteva una frase: attaccare come un giocatore brasiliano, visto che mia mamma è brasiliana, e difendere come un giocatore italiano, perché mio papà è italiano".

It has been revealed that sempre nel periodo al Bologna ha avuto un altro allenatore importante, Thiago Motta, che ha raggiunto risultati incredibili riportando il club in Champions League. "Quando è arrivato c'è stato un bel cambiamento, perché gli allenamenti erano diversi, così come il clima. All'inizio non eravamo partiti benissimo. Poi, pian piano, la squadra ha iniziato a capire le sue richieste. Io ero già andato via quando il Bologna ha raggiunto l'Europa, però già dopo un po' si cominciava a capire quello che chiedeva il mister. Credo che si vedesse fin da subito che, a livello tecnico, fosse un allenatore molto valido. Anche quando i risultati non arrivavano, si capiva che aveva idee ben precise".

Si aspettava di vederlo in difficoltà come è successo alla Juventus? "Sono cose che succedono. Magari a Bologna ha avuto la possibilità di non ottenere subito molti risultati e la città ha avuto pazienza. Alla Juventus, invece, bisogna vincere sempre e subito, quindi forse non ha avuto la stessa possibilità. Credo comunque che in poco tempo troverà sicuramente una sistemazione, perché a livello tecnico è veramente un allenatore valido".

According to recent reports, C'è qualche ex compagno che le è rimasto particolarmente impresso per le sue qualità tecniche? "Credo ne siano passati tanti, anche giocatori che adesso non sono più lì. Per esempio Arnautovic, che considero uno dei più forti con cui abbia giocato. Poi anche Medel, Dominguez, Soriano, Schouten e lo stesso Orsolini, che è ancora lì. Credo ce ne siano stati veramente tanti, non dovrei dimenticare nessuno".

Sources indicate that se le diciamo Zirkzee? "Anche di lui ho bei ricordi. All'inizio magari aveva fatto un po' di fatica a trovare spazio, perché c'era Arnautovic. Poi, nell'anno successivo, ha fatto vedere a tutti il giocatore che è. Ho bei ricordi sia a livello umano sia a livello tecnico, in campo".

Proprio Zirkzee è stato molto cercato quest'estate da diversi club italiani e a gennaio torneranno a farsi avanti squadre come Napoli e Como. C'è una squadra in particolare in cui lo vedresti bene? “Credo che, se viene messo nelle condizioni migliori per rendere in base alle sue qualità, possa fare bene ovunque. È un giocatore con caratteristiche precise e, se una squadra punta su di lui, sicuramente farà vedere il giocatore che è".

Recent findings suggest that tra i giocatori con cui ha condiviso il campo a Bologna c'era anche un giovanissimo Antonio Raimondo, che oggi (purtroppo infortunato) sta facendo molto bene al Frosinone. “Quando ero a Bologna, Raimondo veniva aggregato dalla Primavera alla prima squadra, ma si allenava sempre con noi. Ha esordito proprio quell'anno, credo nel mio primo anno a Bologna. Già durante gli allenamenti si vedeva che era un buon giocatore. Il mister non avrebbe mai portato un ragazzo ad allenarsi sempre con noi e a farlo esordire senza un motivo valido. Magari non ha fatto lo stesso percorso di Zirkzee, ma ha attraversato la Serie B per diversi anni e adesso è arrivato meritatamente a giocare in Serie A".

It has been revealed that ha giocato anche per Empoli, Salernitana e Pisa. Che esperienze sono state? "Di tutte le esperienze cerco sempre di portare con me le cose positive. A Pisa, sicuramente, la vittoria della Serie B: è stato un anno bellissimo sotto tutti i punti di vista, dalla squadra allo staff, fino ai tifosi. È un ricordo che mi porterò dentro per sempre. A Salerno è stato un po' più difficile, però credo che quella piazza meritasse di più. È una grande città, con un tifo incredibile, e io personalmente mi sono trovato bene, anche se quell'anno non è andata bene. Spero che possa tornare a giocare in Serie A nel giro di qualche anno. A Empoli, invece, ricordo soprattutto la prima partita, nella quale ho anche segnato. Un gol all'esordio è qualcosa che ti porti dentro per sempre".

According to recent reports, ha voglia di tornare in Italia? "Adesso cercherò di fare il meglio possibile nei prossimi mesi, qui dove sono. Poi si vedrà. Sicuramente c'è la voglia di tornare a giocare in Italia. Sono ancora di proprietà del Pisa, quindi è una situazione da valutare. Per il momento cerco di dare il meglio qui e poi in futuro vedremo. Se non sarà in Italia, magari sarà da un'altra parte, ma sicuramente c'è l'obiettivo di tornare a giocare in Europa".

Published: 10:38 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 11:29 EST, 23 November 2026.

Bayern Munich have come under criticism from FIFA's players' union and leading figures in the game amid accusations that the club is attempting to slash Jamal Musiala's wages following his diagnosis with a 'neurological dysfunction'.

The Germany international was diagnosed over the summer with absence seizures, a form of epilepsy which causes 'brief but easily treatable seizures'.

Musiala shocked the sporting world when he collapsed in two matches earlier this season, with Bayern manager Vincent Kompany explaining that the player had suffered from a reaction to a change in his medication.

Comments from members of Bayern's hierarchy have sparked controversy in Germany and abroad, with senior figures appearing to question the length of the player's contract – which runs until 2030 – should Musiala not recover his form.

Honorary president Uli Hoeness was the first to speak out on the potential drop-off in form Musiala might suffer with long-term absences, claiming earlier this month that he 'may never regain the performance level he once had'.

'We are facing a dilemma in this case, as he is suffering from an illness that cannot simply be cured, but it can be controlled to a certain extent with the use of medication,' Hoeness told German outlet BR24.

Fifpro and international footballers have come out in support of Musiala over concerns that Bayern Munich might reduce his salary.

Both Uli Hoeness and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge have made comments suggesting consequences should Musiala not return to his level.

Jan-Christian Dreesen also suggested that the club would need to 'assess' the situation if his performances do not return to their high heights.

Chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen then backed up Hoeness's comments and implied that Musiala's contract may need to be 'assessed'.

'We're monitoring his level of play. He'll certainly need time to improve further – like any injured player,' Dreesen noted in discussion with AZ. 'And then we need to calmly assess the situation and, if necessary, sit down with his family and management.

'Either we'll all be happy together and he'll be the same Jamal he always was – or, if he's a different Jamal along the way, we'll have to discuss it.'.

Industry observers note that 'If we're not consistently at a level that also aligns with the economic realities, then we'll have to talk to each other. Nevertheless, we have a valid contract, and that's the end of it.'.

Sources indicate that the 23-year-old is one of Bayern's highest-earners, having signed a deal with the club to extend his time in Bavaria in February 2025. The deal is thought to be worth £18.4million per year.

Adding fuel to the fire days later was former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, who told Sky Sports/RTL that he thought it was almost reasonable to discuss a renegotiation should Musiala not return to the level at which he once played.

According to recent reports, 'That is certainly possible and cannot be ruled out,' he noted. 'Unfortunately, what we know suggests that it will be difficult to reach the level that he has so often shown here in this stadium.'.

It has been revealed that 'We need to talk to the family, the player, and above all, the agency. Because then these sums are – sorry, with all due respect – no longer feasible.

'I can't imagine Jamal leaving the club or another club buying him under these circumstances. That's a problem. I think we handled this very sensitively with the player, and we're all interested in him coming back - ideally in top form. But what happens if that's not the case? Then we'll still have to think about the finances. And that's a task that the board and the supervisory board unfortunately have to make.'.

Rummenigge added that he did not think it was 'problematic' for these discussions to be happening publicly, due to the club's interest in 'him coming back and playing well'.

But the player union Fifpro were forthright in their disagreement with his statements,  releasing a statement claiming that all parties currently sharing their views on Musiala's contract 'should know better'.

'Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession,' the statement read.

Industry observers note that 'In Fifpro's view, this is a co-ordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better.'.

When this statement was shared to social media via journalist Fabrizio Romano, global talents including Jude Bellingham and Musiala's team-mate Michael Olise were among those to like the post.

Musiala collapsed on the pitch at two consecutive games in August (pictured being helped by team-mates against RB Leipzig).

The 23-year-old has been diagnosed with absence seizures and is managing his medication.

Vincent Kompany has been supportive of his player's struggles, and took him off the bench with some success last weekend.

Rio Ferdinand elaborated on those comments in a more detailed post on social media, adding that he believed the club are 'better than this'.

'If they want to negotiate more reasonable terms for the club going forward due to the health challenges Jamal has, then surely speak to him and his team rather than to the media,' Ferdinand wrote on X. 'This situation must be hard enough to deal with for Jamal without the media and club officials talking about it publicly.

Sources indicate that 'Bayern Munich are one of the clubs who from afar have always carried themselves with a class and standard that most have admired. Sadly, this just doesn't feel like Bayern Munich in this situation.'.

Criticisms were even more fiery in Germany, with the vice president of Germany's player union Michael Franz accusing the club of harassment.

It has been revealed that 'What the Bayern Munich officials are doing, and I don't mean Kompany and (Max) Eberl (director of sport), who have behaved impeccably, seems despicable to me,' Franz shared in an interview with Sport1. 'There is even something about it that resembles harassment.'.

'A footballer's level of performance can be discussed publicly, but it is not right to talk about his illness and the salary he receives in such circumstances. We must not forget that Jamal Musiala has done everything in his power to come back.'.

'Money has become more important than the person, and that is unacceptable.'.

Former Bayern captain Stefan Effenberg stressed how important 'support and protection' from the club towards their players is, particularly for those in greater need like Musiala.

Sources indicate that 'We are talking about someone who is suffering from an illness. What I would have expected is for the club's senior officials to apologise,' Effenberg remarked, adding that he thought that the communications from the club had been 'disastrous'.

Musiala collapsed twice within four days in mid-August, first during Bayern's match against Leipzig – shortly after scoring – and then against Heidenheim.

He then returned to the pitch in September, netting against Bodo/Glimt in Champions League action and Union Berlin shortly before the first international break.

After suffering a hamstring injury, Musiala then spent time away from the side before his return at the end of last week – a match which also saw Harry Kane suffer an ankle injury which will keep him out for over three months.

Fifpro's statement went on to add that Bayern must be careful with their player's mental wellbeing as well as his physical concerns.

According to recent reports, 'Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala,' the statement continued. 'Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury.

According to recent reports, 'Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives.

'Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise.'.

Sono arrivate, soprattutto dal punto di vista caratteriale, riportando la concentrazione adeguata almeno per grandi frangenti. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il presidente della Lazio punta a tornare nell’incarico; per i tre posti si presentano anche gli uscenti e Sticchi Damiani.

It has been revealed that la Serie A eleggerà tre consiglieri federali il 14 dicembre, ma i candidati sono cinque. Ai tre uscenti Stefano Campoccia, Giorgio Chiellini e Giuseppe Marotta si sono aggiunti Saverio Sticchi Damiani e il presidente della Lazio Claudio Lotito. Tra le ipotesi in vista del voto c’è anche quella di preferenze disgiunte tra la presidenza FIGC e il Consiglio federale.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Nel breve mandato di Malagò, i posti spettanti alla massima serie erano occupati da Campoccia, dell’Udinese, Chiellini, della Juventus, e Marotta, dell’Inter. Tutti e tre si sono ricandidati. Con loro correranno il presidente del Lecce Sticchi Damiani e Lotito, che punta a tornare nell’incarico già ricoperto.

Come riferisce il Corriere dello Sport, il quadro delle candidature si inserisce in una Serie A attraversata da divisioni. Alcuni club sono usciti dal fronte Malagò, con Atalanta e Inter in testa. Tra gli indecisi figurano anche Juventus e Milan; in vista delle elezioni dei consiglieri federali, le fratture interne potrebbero allargarsi.

Industry observers note that ogni società di Serie A può indicare un candidato al Consiglio federale. Nelle precedenti elezioni Chiellini aveva ottenuto sette voti e Marotta sei, in una situazione descritta come praticamente opposta a quella attuale.

It has been revealed that il fronte favorevole a Galliani, guidato dal presidente interista Marotta, potrebbe risentire della propria posizione di minoranza. I club che sostengono Malagò sono almeno 11: un sostegno necessario alla sua candidatura, per la quale serve l’appoggio di almeno una componente.

In a recent development, in questo scenario, alcune società potrebbero scegliere il voto disgiunto: sostenere un candidato alla presidenza FIGC e, per il Consiglio federale, esprimere una preferenza per un nome non apertamente schierato con lui. L’esempio indicato è un voto per Malagò alla presidenza e per Marotta, primo sostenitore di Galliani, come consigliere. Una soluzione che richiederebbe un lavoro diplomatico.

Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

According to recent reports, it was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes demonstrated he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

According to recent reports, the one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward rapidly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n.

Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

Industry observers note that you would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they demonstrated to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA.

Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

It has been revealed that leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6.

It has been revealed that it was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

Industry observers note that the misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

It has been revealed that decent enough watch for roughly half the game, settled on a shoot-out in which Alex Cairns got nowhere near any of Manchester United’s penalties. Doubt he will lose much sleep over it. Bruno Fernandes grinned broadly when he missed.

Give the wrong man a microphone and chaos will ensue. On this evidence he might be worth a punt for goals and assists topping 25 this season like they did in 2024-25 for Brentford. Though he may have to take pens off Bruno Fernandes to get there.

Amass tries to play a one-two with Zirkzee but the crucial middle pass of the three, from Zirkzee, goes astray.

Bikol heads Longstaff’s free-kick from the right over the bar after clever work from Bogle to earn the opportunity. .

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

It has been revealed that it’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in New Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

While Leeds will have newly introduced signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Giornata di cambiamenti sulle panchine di Serie B. L'Arezzo ha ufficializzato l'esonero di Cristian Bucchi e del suo staff tecnico, individuando in Fabio Caserta il possibile successore. Novità anche in casa Empoli, dove Lorenzo Tonelli è stato nominato nuovo allenatore della prima squadra.

L'Arezzo ha comunicato di aver sollevato dall'incarico di allenatore della Prima Squadra Cristian Bucchi e i componenti del suo staff tecnico. Nel comunicato, il club ha ringraziato il tecnico per la professionalità, la dedizione e l'impegno dimostrati, ricordando soprattutto la vittoria del campionato e il ritorno in Serie B, traguardo che rappresenta una delle pagine più importanti della storia recente amaranto.

La separazione era nell'aria e la società ha già individuato il nome del successore: sarà Fabio Caserta a guidare la squadra nel prosieguo della stagione. L'accordo tra le parti è stato raggiunto e il nuovo allenatore è atteso in città oggi, venerdì 27 novembre. Per lui ci sarà subito un impegno importante: il debutto è infatti in programma domenica 29 novembre, quando l'Arezzo affronterà il Pisa. Lo riporta Sky.

It has been revealed that L'altra notizia di giornata arriva da Empoli. Il club azzurro ha annunciato che, a partire dalla prossima sfida contro l'Hellas Verona, sarà Lorenzo Tonelli a guidare la prima squadra. Il tecnico, che ha allenato la formazione Under 17, dirigerà il primo allenamento questo pomeriggio al Sussidiario del Carlo Castellani Computer Gross Arena. Nel suo staff entrerà anche Francesco Tavano, con il ruolo di collaboratore tecnico.

In a recent development, resta da considerare la questione del patentino: Tonelli è in possesso della licenza UEFA A, che non consente di allenare da primo allenatore una squadra di Serie B. Per questo è necessaria una deroga, arrivata alla luce della comunicazione ufficiale dell'Empoli, ma valida soltanto per i prossimi 30 giorni.

Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.

Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.

The visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box. Jimenez and his wife marked his return to Molineux by giving 5,000 fans black scarves emblazoned with the words ‘Si Senor’ - a nod to his song - and Jimenez did not disappoint as he rifled in his penalty.

Sources indicate that LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU.

Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

Peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

Industry observers note that “We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

“We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”.

Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

Mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

Industry observers note that “Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we demonstrated there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”.

The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

However, Wolves scored the first goal of the upcoming campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

"A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq.

Blackburn drew level through an unlikely source just nine minutes later as McLoughlin headed in his first-ever goal in English football in more than 150 games when he met Ryoya Morishita’s cross from the right at the near post.

The home side had chances to retake the lead before the break as Lopez curled a shot narrowly over the top from 20-yards while Kieran Trippier teed up Mateus Mane for a chance as the teenager found the top of the net from distance.

Blackburn turned the game on its head minutes after the break as Gudjohnsen turned home Afolayan’s deflected ball in from the right from close range to stun Molineux into silence.

"It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK.

Peixoto introduced Jimenez from the bench on the hour mark but even the Mexican could not lift Wolves with Blackburn comfortable for long periods as frustration grew in the stands.

However, Alebiosu handled Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross from the left in injury time and the referee awarded a spot kick which allowed Jimenez to mark his Wolves return with an equaliser from 12-yards as he sent Balazs Toth the wrong way.

“I think it is a really harsh one. He [the referee] has to be sure at such a critical time of the game. And I do not think he can be sure. I think he has almost had a guess that he is in the box. It is such a substantial call.”.

According to recent reports, “We see the ref’s position. The fact the ref makes the decision to give the penalty in my opinion, it is a bigger decision to give it then to not. We have got the luxury of the replays and we are still not sure. His whole body is outside the box.”.

“It looks outside the box to me [the penalty incident]. The still picture suggests to me it was outside the box. We can get better and we will have to. We have to be more dominant with the ball at times and be better in attack. We have done a lot of work on that in pre-season. When Wolverhampton Wanderers last attacked the Championship under a Portuguese manager new to English football, it proved a vintage season.

Molineux was under the spell of Nuno Espírito Santo in that 2017-18 campaign, and the massive question is whether César Peixoto can lead a repeat nearly a decade later.

Peixoto was a surprise appointment in June, replacing Rob Edwards, and he has been entrusted with the mission of returning Wolves to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

“I have changed some things with set-pieces and some things in other moments of the game because I want the team to be organised and understand all the different moments within a match. During pre-season we have scored some goals from high pressing, but we will not be able to press high in every moment of every game. The players have to understand the game and recognise what each moment requires. It is important that we work as a team. When we can press high, we’ll press high. When we need to defend in a mid-block, we will stay organised. When the opposition pushes us deeper, which will sometimes happen, we have to be organised there as well.

It has been revealed that “There are a lot of crosses in the Championship, for example, so the team needs to understand what to do in those situations. We want to play our football, be offensive and react strongly when we lose the ball, but we also need to understand the different moments of the game. I think we are at a good level to attack the Championship.”.

The 2026/27 Championship season kicks off at Molineux as Wolves host Blackburn, with the home side hoping to put the bad memories of last season firmly behind them. There are newly introduced playoff rules in place for this season, with six places now up for grabs in the play-offs.

Recent findings suggest that wolves are aiming to return to the Premier League at the first attempt, having endured a miserable season in the top flight last year as they finished bottom with just three wins to their name. It has been a summer of change at the club as they chose to change managers. Rob Edwards lost his job in what was a shock move and was replaced by 46-year-old Cesar Peixoto, with this being his first head coaching position outside of his home country Portugal. Back in 2017/18, Wolves won the Championship title led by Peixoto’s compatriot Nuno Espirito Santo.

In a recent development, “I am ready,” Peixoto told Wolves’ club website. “We have worked very hard during pre-season, and I think we have had a great pre-season. All the players have worked very, very hard and they understand what I want from them. I am ready and confident going into the first game. Football is football, whether it is in Portugal or England, but there are different characteristics to the game here. We have watched, observed and analysed the Championship. We did that work before I came to the club, so we know what to expect.

“It is going to be a tough season with good teams, but we are prepared to fight for the three points game after game and week after week. We know what we want from the team and we know what our massive goal is. We’re going to work very hard and fight to achieve that goal.”.

Recent findings suggest that they have brought in vast experience on the player side in the shape of Kieran Trippier and Raul Jimenez, who is back at Molineux three years after leaving for Fulham. Although they have lost Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes to Aston Villa, most of their squad has stayed intact as they pursue promotion back to the top flight. It is a special year for the club as they celebrate their 150th anniversary.

Blackburn, led by experienced manager Tony Mowbray, did not enjoy a great season in the Championship last year, finishing down in 20th place and just five points above the relegation zone. 14 years have now passed since Blackburn last played in the top flight.

“I think it is a tough start,” Mowbray mentioned. “On paper, I would suggest the first couple of games, particularly, jumped out as a tough start. One of the Premier League sides from last season, away from home. They have got a very talented squad, a pretty expensive squad. They have got some very good individual talent. Yet, there is an argument to say they have not won many football matches in the last calendar year. So, what we get, we will have to wait and see.”.

These sides last met in the FA Cup during the 2024/25 season, with Wolves winning that fourth-round tie 2-0 thanks to goals from Matheus Cunha and Gomes, both of whom are now plying their trade elsewhere. The omens would appear to be on Wolves’ side as they are unbeaten in their last eight league meetings with Blackburn. Both sides progressed to the second round of the League Cup last weekend, with Wolves beating Port Vale 3-0 and Blackburn overcoming Burton Albion 2-1.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

La campagna coinvolge sei calciatori e calciatrici delle Nazionali e rinnova l’invito a comporre il 1522.

Industry observers note that la FIGC rinnova il suo impegno contro la violenza sulle donne con una campagna di sensibilizzazione affidata a sei calciatori e calciatrici e ribadisce l’invito alle vittime di violenza o stalking a chiamare il 1522. Secondo quanto riportato da Figc, L’iniziativa è legata alla Giornata internazionale per l’eliminazione della violenza sulle donne. Lo riferisce la FIGC.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Gianluigi Donnarumma, Cristiana Girelli, Laura Giuliani, Pio Esposito, Riccardo Calafiori e Annamaria Serturini sono i protagonisti della comunicazione della Federazione. La campagna affronta la violenza di genere in tutte le sue forme: non soltanto gli episodi di cronaca, ancora troppo frequenti, ma anche la dimensione culturale e sociale del fenomeno, legata agli stereotipi e al mancato riconoscimento della libertà e dell’autonomia delle donne.

Recent findings suggest that il messaggio distingue la violenza da ciò che può essere presentato come una lite, il controllo dalla gelosia e il possesso dalla protezione: «È una lite? No, è violenza. È gelosia? No, è controllo. È protezione? No, è possesso». A queste domande la campagna affianca una risposta: il numero 1522.

Il 1522 è un servizio gratuito di pubblica utilità istituito nel 2006 dal Dipartimento per le Pari Opportunità. Il suo obiettivo è favorire l’emersione e il contrasto della violenza contro le donne, sia all’interno sia all’esterno della famiglia, attraverso un’ampia azione di sistema.

In occasione della Giornata internazionale, la FIGC torna quindi a invitare le vittime di ogni forma di violenza o stalking a comporre il numero.

Chelsea's slump in form unpacked: The stars who badly need to step up from Emi Martinez to Cole Palmer, what defensive horror highlights mean for Xabi Alonso's job security - and the players in line to leave in January

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1370 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:02 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Chelsea are lurching towards a crisis after yet another loss in which they were bullied, this time by Leeds United.
  • That 4-1 hiding saw Xabi Alonso heckled, and his players booed at both half-time and full-time, arguably deservedly so for such a disastrous showing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 12:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:02 EST, 23 November 2026.

Chelsea are lurching towards a crisis after yet another loss in which they were bullied, this time by Leeds United.

That 4-1 hiding saw Xabi Alonso heckled, and his players booed at both half-time and full-time, arguably deservedly so for such a disastrous showing.

It has led to tentative speculation around Alonso's future as Chelsea prepare to travel to Oliver Glasner's Nottingham Forest on Friday night, not to mention questions about where he is going wrong and how he might arrest his team's slump in form.

Here, Daily Mail Sport tackles all the burning issues at Stamford Bridge...

Sources indicate that chief among Chelsea’s problems is the fact they have conceded 20 Premier League goals this season. It is as many as they have scored at the other end. So, as much as we have enjoyed their freescoring forward line this season, so too must we criticise their disastrous defending.

Recent findings suggest that we know Alonso can organise a defence. His Bayer Leverkusen side only conceded 24 goals when they won the Bundesliga as unbeaten champions in 2023-24. Chelsea are now on the verge of overtaking that total before we even hit December.

Liam Delap, their former striker now at Forest, will be desperate to add to that tally this Friday, too.

Xabi Alonso is coming under growing pressure, with his Chelsea side failing to back up their promising early-season form.

Levi Colwill was all at sea against Leeds as Chelsea shipped another four goals, taking their tally to 20 in 11 games.

In a recent development, this morning, I watched back all 20 of the goals that Chelsea have leaked this term. There have been so many individual mistakes.

Recent findings suggest that like on day one, in the 3-2 win at Fulham, when an out of position Robert Sanchez let in Josh King's shot. And when Levi Colwill missed a defensive header which should have been routine, which led to Gonzalo Garcia scoring.

Chelsea got rid of Sanchez after that game, but Emiliano Martinez has hardly helped shore up this defence, as was apparent in the 4-1 loss to Leeds, when Colwill and Co were again all over the shop.

Until they cut out the silly mistakes, it is hard to see Chelsea competing at the top end of the Premier League.

In a recent development, every manager at every club is sackable. Nobody is immune. But that’s not to say Alonso is suddenly up for the chop at Chelsea. I haven’t heard anything which would suggest those inside the club think finding a fourth permanent manager in the year 2026 is the answer.

Let’s not forget the overwhelming optimism when news broke of Chelsea striking an agreement to hire Alonso. It was an hour or so after the club had lost the 2026 FA Cup final to Manchester City. Recently, I took a look at the comments section of the story I wrote that day. It was full of excitement from Chelsea fans, and anger from Liverpool supporters at missing out on him.

According to recent reports, anyway, I think it’s too soon for us to start talking about Alonso’s job. He is in a bad moment, obviously. A very bad moment. Losing at home to Tottenham Hotspur and Leeds is a complete no-no for any Blues boss.

The supporters are more likely to curse his name than chant it right now, and it is hard to identify the style Alonso wants, with few discernible patterns of play to Chelsea's football.

But let’s give the bloke a chance to get himself out of this jam as he heads into his 12th Premier League match.

According to recent reports, believe it or not, Chelsea don’t like changing managers mid-season if they can help it. Enzo Maresca resigned, exiting on January 1, 2026. Liam Rosenior was sacked, yes, but the club were effectively forced into that change as the players clearly gave up on him. Let’s see if Alonso can find some solutions.

Chelsea don’t like changing managers mid-season if they can help it and Alonso, remember, has only had 11 Premier League games in charge.

We’ve tried to coax a little anger out of Alonso at press conferences, practically encouraging him to have a pop at his players for how they are performing, but he tends to resist the urge.

Sources indicate that he’s clearly a nice guy. However, a Chelsea source does tell me he’s different behind the scenes. We may not see it on the outside, but internally, he is perfectly capable of being fiery with the players.

Recent findings suggest that which I hope is the case. Because sometimes, it can feel as if these Chelsea players need a good kick up the backside, rather than being coddled.

I wrote a piece after the 4-1 loss to Leeds about how superstars can be stroppy. It’s normal. They can be so good that when the game isn’t going their way, they show their sulky side.

Palmer did that both during and after Saturday’s defeat. It was pretty poor from him to not want to go around applauding the fans who had bothered to stick around at full-time, even if there had been boos. An apology has been attributed to Palmer on social media, but that’s just another case of fake quotes being circulated.

Industry observers note that for me, Palmer has to look at himself as much as anybody. It’s been too long since we’ve seen him try to take a match by the scruff of the neck.

Cole Palmer put in another quiet display against Leeds - he needs to start taking matches by the scruff of the neck.

WHAT HAPPENED WITH EMEGHA AFTER THE GAME?

It has been revealed that striker Emmanuel Emegha started for the first time and scored for the first time in Chelsea’s 4-1 loss to Leeds. Then he exited Stamford Bridge.

We have seen players leaving the stadium on foot before. Videos of Palmer being surrounded by supporters while being escorted to his ride home occasionally crop up on social media.

Sources indicate that emegha had possessions stolen from his car while he was in a restaurant after the match and the incident has been reported to police. He was not harmed.

From a footballing point of view, I'd like to see Emegha start away at Forest this Friday.

Not that I’m aware. He’s been linked with Paris Saint-Germain and I had an email from a PR person this morning trying to push a loan to AC Milan or Roma as a possibility.

Recent findings suggest that alonso has given the fans what they wanted in the last few league games. He started Estevao against Manchester United, brought him on at half-time at Sunderland and started him against Leeds.

Estevao, clearly an exciting talent, could do with taking these opportunities to show why he deserves more of them.

Estevao has been given a chance to shine by Alonso in recent weeks but has failed to grab his opportunities.

I could see Malo Gusto leaving if there’s interest and Chelsea don’t keep demanding £75million, because it is hard to see who would spend that on him.

Gusto started in five of Alonso’s first six games in all competitions at the beginning of the campaign. Since then, he has been handed one start in eight, and that was in the Carabao Cup at Liverpool. Coming on as a substitute in the loss to Leeds, he tried and failed to play Brenden Aaronson offside and was then beaten by his man as the visitors made it 4-1.

I wouldn’t be surprised if a few other fringe players are linked with leaving in pursuit of game time ahead of January, such as Valentin Barco and Jamie Gittens, who is training again after his ankle injury.

As for incomings, I don’t need to tell you that Chelsea are interested in Alex Scott of Bournemouth. Arsenal are, too, but the word is the Blues are still the frontrunners as we approach January. Whether Scott is what this team needs is another conversation.

La Lazio si prepara a ritrovare i suoi tifosi: circa 40mila sono attesi all’Olimpico per il derby del 13 dicembre e altri 20mila a Milano per la Supercoppa contro l’Inter, in programma il 22 dicembre. Secondo quanto riportato da la Repubblica, Intanto Curva Nord e distinti sono già esauriti per la gara con l’Atalanta del 6 dicembre.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Per Gattuso il ritorno del pubblico nello stadio di casa riguarda, almeno, le sfide con l’Atalanta e con la Roma.

Industry observers note that per la stracittadina sono previsti circa 40mila laziali all’Olimpico. La previsione per la Supercoppa contro l’Inter è invece di 20mila tifosi a Milano. Nella gara del 22 dicembre la Lazio proverà a conquistare il diciassettesimo trofeo della sua storia.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Roma, il capitano della Lazio incontra gli alunni della scuola primaria Pistelli vincitrice del contest nazionale “AttiviAMOci tutti i giorni in movimento”. Tra gioco, movimento e storie personali, un messaggio: nello sport, come nella vita, la ver.

In a recent development, ROMA – Gol al novantesimo o weekend senza compiti? Derby vinto o 10 in matematica? Questa volta la sfida si gioca tra i banchi di scuola e a scendere in campo è Mattia Zaccagni. Il capitano della Lazio incontra i bambini della Scuola Primaria Pistelli di Roma per una partita speciale a colpi di “Questo o quello?”, tra domande a sorpresa, risposte istintive e qualche scelta davvero difficile.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Industry observers note that L’appuntamento fa parte del percorso nazionale promosso da Sport e Salute e adidas per contrastare il drop-out sportivo e tenere viva, fin dai primi anni, la voglia di fare sport. E la Pistelli non è una scuola qualsiasi: istituto aderente a Scuola Attiva Kids, è stata protagonista del contest nazionale “AttiviAMOci tutti i giorni in movimento”, conquistando il primo posto grazie al percorso realizzato per promuovere il movimento come parte integrante della quotidianità scolastica. Una comunità che ha scelto di fare dello sport un’abitudine, un’opportunità e un’esperienza da condividere.

It has been revealed that È proprio da questa energia che prende vita l’incontro con Zaccagni. I bambini diventano arbitri delle scelte, mentre il campione si mette alla prova: gol decisivo o vacanza più lunga? Una partita vinta o un bel voto a scuola? Ma dietro le risate e le risposte più divertenti c’è anche spazio per qualcosa di più profondo. Perché lo sport non è soltanto il momento della vittoria: è imparare a gestire una sconfitta, superare un errore, affrontare una difficoltà e trovare ogni volta la voglia di ripartire.

Industry observers note that «Nel calcio, come nella vita, ci sono momenti in cui le cose non vanno come vorresti. Puoi sbagliare un gol, perdere una partita o attraversare un periodo complicato. Ma è proprio in quei momenti che devi trovare la forza di rialzarti, continuare a lavorare e credere nelle tue capacità. Io ho imparato che non si cresce soltanto quando si vince, ma soprattutto quando si riesce a reagire alle difficoltà. Ai ragazzi dico di divertirsi, di non avere paura di sbagliare e di non mollare mai quello che li fa stare bene. Perché nello sport, prima ancora dei risultati, conta la voglia di continuare a giocare», racconta Mattia Zaccagni ai bambini.

It has been revealed that dalle parole si passa al movimento. Con i tutor di Sport e Salute, gli alunni partecipano a una lezione di attività motoria, tra giochi, prove di abilità e lavoro di squadra. Tutti protagonisti, ciascuno con le proprie capacità, in un’esperienza che mette al centro il piacere di muoversi e stare insieme.

Sources indicate that È questa la sfida che Sport e Salute e adidas vogliono vincere: contrastare l’abbandono sportivo, offrendo ai più giovani occasioni per scoprire una passione, sentirsi parte di una squadra e trovare nello sport uno spazio in cui crescere. Perché nessuno dovrebbe smettere di giocare solo perché non è il più bravo, perché ha incontrato una difficoltà o perché una partita è andata male.

According to recent reports, la Pistelli, con il suo percorso premiato a livello nazionale, dimostra che questa partita può iniziare proprio dalla scuola. E che il risultato più importante non è segnare un gol in più, ma fare in modo che domani ci siano ancora tanti bambini pronti a scendere in campo.

Newcastle kit fiasco sums up haphazard pre-season

📅 15 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2494 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.
  • The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.
  • During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in new manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

Recent findings suggest that jaissle’s team found their feet as the first 45 minutes progressed, with Yoane Wissa their biggest attacking threat. The striker endured a difficult first season at the club, but his performances at the World Cup with DR Congo appear to have restored confidence.

Sources indicate that newcastle were level just before half-time, when Malick Thiaw rose highest to plant home a back-post header from a corner. Former Brentford goalkeeper Mark Flekken appealed in vain for a foul, but there was no infringement.

After changing all 10 outfield players at half-time against Everton, Jaissle was more circumspect with second-half substitutes; Rory Finneran for Lewis Miley was the only change before the 80th minute.

It has been revealed that newcastle faded though, and the game was won by Victor Boniface scoring just a few minutes after coming on as a substitute. The Nigeria striker wrong-footed Sean Steur with an impudent piece of skill before rolling the ball into the bottom corner.

The North-East club are coming to terms with the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães this summer, as well as manager Eddie Howe. They have one more pre-season friendly to play, against Strasbourg on Sunday, before they begin their Premier League campaign at home to Liverpool.

Newcastle United (4-2-3-1) Hornicek; M Miley (Pivas 81), Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley (Finneran h-t); Elanga, Woltemade (Neave 86), Barnes; Wissa. Subs Charlton, Harris (g), Sanusi, Johnson.

Bayer Leverkusen (4-2-3-1) Flekken; Vazquez (Tape h-t), Bade, Tapsoba, Gutierrez (Belocian 70); Garcia, Fernandez (Terrier 70); Maza (Boniface 80), Tillman (Doganay 70), Moreira (Tella 80); Kofane (Schick h-t). Subs Hofmann, Arthur, Oermann, Poku, Blaswich (g), Alfa-Ruprecht, Hawighorst, Lomb (g).

Referee Michael Oliver (Durham). Attendance 39,059.

A second pre-season defeat in a week for Newcastle. Just like against Everton, they faded in the second 45 minutes but Jaissle decided to leave some tired legs out there for fitness purposes. The performances of Barnes and Wissa were promising, but Newcaslte are giving up chances.

Newcastle had a free-kick with the last kick of the game, but Harvey Barnes loops the delivery straight into Flekken’s gloves.

Schik with a chance to wrap up the victory, but Hornicek saves before Thiaw clears to deny Terrier a tap in on the rebounds.

There will be just three minutes of added time to play.

Elanga fouled near the touchline, but time is running out. The free-kick won by Neave came to nothing.

Sources indicate that chance for Barnes! Good combination play involving Elanga and Wissa down the right, and the ball flashed across the six-yard box. Barnes almost steered it in, but did not make firm enough contact.

Industry observers note that newcastle attacking with more urgency since conceding, but there are moans and groans in the ground at a misplaced Elanga pass. Sean Neave has just replaced Woltemade, and the 19-year-old wins a free-kick in a crossing position with his first action of the game.

The striker has only been on the pitch a few minutes, but Boniface has restored Leverkusen’s lead. Lovely chop inside the box, which sent Steur for a hot dog, before passing the ball into the far corner. No celebration of note from a player who could be on the move this summer.

Newcastle making just their second change of the game: Pivas replaces Mason Miley at right-back.

Leverkusen have made two more changes: Moreira and Maza off, Tella and Boniface on.

The corner is straight down the throat of Flekken, and that prompsts some groans from the home fans.

In a recent development, newcastle having to defend deep for long periods, but Elanga did well to win a free-kick with little support. Moreira dragged the winger down. Then Wissa’s cross is turned behind for a corner.

In a recent development, woltemade’s control lets him down as he tries to bring the ball down on halfway. The game is being played at a snail’s pace at the moment, but Leverkusen are dominating the ball.

It has been revealed that play has now resumed. Garcia does well to defend after Lewis Hall won the ball back in a dangerous position.

According to recent reports, time for another hydration break and Leverkusen are making three more substitutions. We await further changes from Jaissle. Should the game finish level, there will be a penalty shoot-out to decide the winner of the Visit Malta Cup.

Rather like the mid-week friendly against Everton, Newcastle have faded after half-time. Struggling to get into the game in any meaningful way. Slick football from Leverkusen but Fernandez fails to bring the ball under his spell in the box when there was time and space to shoot.

Recent findings suggest that leverkusen just inches away from regaining the lead. It was an incisive run off the left from Afonso Moreira, who tried to place the ball into the far corner but his attempt rolled just wide of the post.

Good defensive header by Lewis Hall before Wissa wins a foul on halfway. Newcastle feeding off scraps at the moment. Elanga goes too early and is flagged offside.

Recent findings suggest that bayer Leverkusen have had the better of it in this half, but some of the shooting has been wayward. This time is it Schik’s turn to slash a shot over the bar. Fouls committed by Finneran and Botman.

Sources indicate that newcastle with a three-on-three on the break after Wissa does well to win the ball back on halfway, but Woltemade was too slow to get his shot away at the end of the move. More good play from Wissa.

Half a chance for Fernandez to shoot from the edge of the D, but he was leaning back and ballooned the shot miles over the bar.

Finneran, the youngster in Newcastle’s midfield, is caught on the ball but then does well to recover it. I reckon there will be a raft of changes on the hour mark.

It has been revealed that corner for Leverkusen after Moreira gets forward and attacks Mason Miley. The German side have additional aerial threat with Schik on the pitch. Woltemade does well to head clear.

Bayer Leverkuen kick off in the second half.

Jaissle made 10 against Everton, so wants his starters to build minutes today. Rory Finneran is coming on for Newcastle, an 18-year-old academy player. He replaces Lewis Miley in midfield. Czech striker Patrik Schik is on for Bayer Leverkusen.

Sources indicate that the scoreline is a fair reflection of an even first half, with Wissa Newcastle’s best player. The story though, is that kit clash that prompted Newcastle to change into their lilac third kit halfway through the half.

Just the two minutes of stoppage time to play.

In a recent development, newcastle equalise from a set-piece. Flekken is claiming a foul, but it is a legitimate goal. The goalkeeper was nowhere to be seen on a corner that looped all the way to be back post, and he seemed to lose his bearings allowing Thiaw to find the far corner.

Sources indicate that newcastle have a corner after another move in which Wissa was lively. His performances have been a ray of light in pre-season, he really struggled in his first season at the club.

According to recent reports, lewis Hall takes the free-kick, but he scoops it well over the bar. Elanga delivers a low cross from the right, but Garcia is well positioned to clear.

Newcastle enjoying a lot more possession now, but you cannot say they look like equalising.

That was better though, more zip in the attack with Elanga laying the ball off for Wissa and Fernandez is booked from dragging the Newcastle forward to the ground. Free-kick in a shooting position.

In a recent development, good play from Lewis Hall, skipping beyond two challenges to escape from a tight spot but then his crossfield pass is intercepted. Moreira passes the ball straight out of play for a Newcastle goal kick, when there was a chance for Leverkusen to punish the hosts on the break.

Elanga tries to take on Gutierrez but his low cross is too close to Flekken. Gutierrez then buys a foul when under pressure from Lewis Miley. Game has become quite bitty following those stoppages. Maza then chops down Harvery Barnes.

Recent findings suggest that the game is back under way. Changing kits has improved things visually but it is still not ideal. You wonder how on earth two clubs of this stature failed to liaise on this before the game.

Bayer Leverkusen are still on top, but play has been stopped for a hydration break. Some boos from the stands, it is not an especially hot day.

According to recent reports, on the subject of the kit clash, Newcastle are now changing into their lilac away kit. Shades of Manchester United at the Dell all those years ago.

A short stoppage in play after Tapsoba receives a knock in the small of the back from Newcastle’s goalkeeper Hornicek. Both managers get their players over for a tactical conflab.

Leverkusen look very accomplished in possession, they are moving the ball well through the lines. Kofane was a big threat when they played Arsenal in last season’s Champions League and they are looking to find him with crosses. Mason Miley defends well at right-back, but at the expense of a corner.

Flekken called into action again, Newcastle starting to warm to their task. It was direct play from first Elanga and then Barnes, but his cross deflects towards the goalkeeper and he parries away. Then Barnes is fouled, and Newcastle have a free-kick in a crossing position near the left corner of the penalty area. Poor delivery from Barnes, Flekken claims.

Newcastle fans sing “walking in a Keegan wonderland” in unison. Bade is then penalised for catching Woltemade late as they contested an aerial challenge.

Newcastle’s best moment so far: Wissa peels off the shoulder of Bade and tested Flekken with a volley from a tight angle. The goalkeeper saved and Leverkusen scramble clear, but it was good movement from the Newcastle striker.

Sources indicate that leverkusen continue to make the running, enjoying more possession and most of it is coming inside Newcastle’s half. Goalkeeper Flekken takes a beat inside his own six-yard box, and his pass out is almost cut out by Woltemade.

Newcastle’s players are wearing black armbands in memory of Kevin Keegan.

There is a slightly awkward clash of kits on display: both shirts feature a lot of white, and the blue trim around the shoulders of Newcastle’s home kit is quite similar to Leverkusen’s away strip.

Kofane, who impressed up front last season in Germany, throws himself at a cross.

Fans were barely settled in their seats when Maza’s vicious left-footed strike from outside of the area flew past Hornicek. Cracking goal, not much the goalkeeper could do about it.

Newcastle get the game under way.

According to recent reports, matthias Jaissle walks to the home dugout for the first time as manager. Just eight days until the proper stuff begins against Liverpool, a fixture which tends to throw up entertaining games. Bayer Leverkusen keep the home players waiting in the tunnel.

Sources indicate that the former Liverpool defender has been linked with a move to Arsenal this week. Quansah is with his team-mates but not part of the matchday squad.

Bayer Leverkusen XI: Flekken; Gutierrez, Bade, Fernandez, Moreira, Tillman, Tapsoba, Arthur, Garcia, Maza, Kofane.

Subs: Blaswich, Lomb, Hofmann, Terrier, Schick, Oermann, Tape, Poku, Vazquez, Boniface, Tella, Alfa-Ruprecht, Doganay, Hawighorst.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; M Miley, Thiaw (c), Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley; Elanga, Woltemade, Barnes; Wissa.

Subs: Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Sanusi, Johnson, Finneran, Neave.

Today's team to take on Bayer Leverkusen in the @VisitMalta Weekender 👊 pic.twitter.com/ZfRvucBXSq.

Newcastle United continue their preparations for the latest season with a home friendly against Bayer Leverkusen, hoping to improve on their pretty limp showing against Everton at Murrayfield.

Sources indicate that newly introduced manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the Premier League season, insisting that he sees opportunity in the situation. Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who had lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a significant challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle remarked.

Sources indicate that “We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”.

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about fresh signings.

It has been revealed that “Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”.

Jaissle remarked he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

Industry observers note that “The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he stated.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”.

Le dichiarazioni dell'ex team manager della Lazio sul cammino in campionato.

Compleanno dolce per Maurizio Manzini, storico team manager della Lazio, intervenuto a Radiosei durante ‘NMM‘  per commentare il momento positivo dei biancocelesti.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Sources indicate that questo mio compleanno lo festeggio in un momento piacevole dal punto di vista sportivo. È orgoglio vedere la Lazio lì in classifica, grazie al lavoro di Rino e della squadra. È un grande merito loro ed una grande soddisfazione per noi. Come andrà a finire la stagione? Non lo dico per scaramanzia, diciamo che speriamo di salvarci.

Il legame tra Maurizio Manzini e il club capitolino nasce da lontano, già nel 1971, quando da dirigente nel settore dell'aviazione iniziò a supportare volontariamente la società nella gestione logistica e delle trasferte, conquistando la stima di figure leggendarie come Tommaso Maestrelli. Dopo un primo rifiuto, nella stagione 1988/89 accettò ufficialmente l'incarico di team manager, diventando per decenni l'anello di congiunzione indispensabile tra spogliatoio e vertici societari. Poliglotta, apprezzato da arbitri, colleghi e persino dagli avversari per stile e riservatezza, ha rappresentato la memoria storica del club fino al graduale passaggio di consegne avvenuto a partire dall'annata 2014/15.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By ISABEL BALDWIN, US ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 10:23 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 13:19 EST, 23 November 2026.

The World Cup is set to return to America after FIFA awarded the 2031 women's tournament to a historic four-nation bid.

Following the success of the men's tournament this summer, the United States was announced as one of the hosts of the women's edition in five years' time during a virtual meeting of FIFA's national associations on Monday.

The US will co-host the global soccer extravaganza alongside Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica after the four countries' joint bid was awarded uncontested the 2031 tournament.

The selection marks a milestone for the Women's World Cup with the tournament being hosted across four nations for the first time in its history.

The last World Cup was co-hosted by multiple countries for the first time with the 2023 edition taking place across Australia and New Zealand.

This summer's men's World Cup was also co-hosted by the US with games taking place across the States, Canada and Mexico.

The World Cup is set to return to the United States for the 2031 women's edition of the event.

Spain are reigning champions after winning the Women's World Cup in 2023.

The United States Women's National Team are four-time winners in 1991, 1999, 2015 and 2019.

The 2031 tournament will also be the largest in the competition's history, featuring an expanded 48-team field and 104 matches for the first time.

'We are incredibly honored and excited to welcome the world to the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica for the 2031 FIFA Women's World Cup,' remarked US Soccer President Cindy Parlow Cone.

'This is a historic moment for our four countries, but the opportunity is much bigger than any one of us. Together with FIFA, we want to deliver the biggest and most impactful Women's World Cup in history and use its success to accelerate the growth of women's soccer around the world. Our ambition is to create a tournament that not only inspires millions of players, but helps give them the opportunities to play, grow and pursue their dreams.'.

Industry observers note that the selection marks the third time that the Women's World Cup has been awarded to the US with the country previously hosting the landmark 1999 and 2003 editions alone. The national team's tournament win in 1999 was the second of its four titles.

Meanwhile, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will become first-time hosts at the historic tournament.

'This milestone furthers the continued belief that the best days of soccer in America are still ahead,' said U.S. Soccer CEO and General Secretary JT Batson.

'We have an opportunity to use the momentum from the 2031 FIFA Women's World Cup to accelerate our ambitions for the future of soccer, from expanding access and participation to strengthening the pathways that develop the next generation of players. We are excited to work alongside our partners across the region to make this tournament a defining moment for women's soccer.'.

The U.S.-led 2031 project across the CONCACAF regional soccer body bid offers FIFA a choice of stadiums in 20 cities: 14 in the U.S., four in Mexico plus San José in Costa Rica and Kingston, Jamaica.

US Soccer President Cindy Parlow Cone noted the federation was honored to be selected.

The host selection of the 2035 Women's World Cup was awarded to a joint bid between England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.

The host selection of the 2035 Women's World Cup was also announced on Monday with the tournament being awarded to another joint bid between England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.

It marks the first time that a World Cup has been hosted on the British Isles since the men's tournament in 1966 in England.

The United Kingdom bid joins England with Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales that offers a choice from 19 venues, including Wembley Stadium in London.

The winning candidates and FIFA president Gianni Infantino promised commercially successful tournaments - the first editions with 48 teams and 104 games - and to reinvest all that money in women's soccer.

It has been revealed that FIFA wanted these heavyweights of women's soccer to face no opposition without rival bids and so lead hosting the first expanded tournaments. That will bring parity with the men's World Cup which expanded to 48 teams this year in the US, Canada and Mexico.

The 2027 Women's World Cup will have 32 teams in Brazil.

Recent findings suggest that pep Guardiola, allenatore, ha rilasciato un’intervista a Romario a Romario Tv: “È uno dei miei più grandi onori che hanno pensato a me per allenare la nazionale italiana, ma sentivo di dovermi fermare. Se me ne avevano parlato anni prima, probabilmente avrei accettato, ma all’epoca, con Paolo Maldini e Leonardo, mi sono reso conto che dovevo fermarmi. Avevo bisogno di più tempo per me stesso. Sono stato allenatore per 18 anni, allenando ogni tre giorni. È la prima volta che ne parlo, ma mi vergognavo di aver detto di no a un Paese come l’Italia. In nazionale il tempo è limitato. Ancelotti? Lui si adatta a questi tempi più ristretti. Ma non potrei mai dubitare delle capacità di Carlo. È impossibile, perché lo conosco. È un leader nella gestione del gruppo. Dicono che sia il numero uno. L’ho affrontato, è molto intuitivo, intelligente nelle sue decisioni tattiche. Poi sa anche lui che se non vinci non duri. Il Portogallo deve dargli l’addio che merita. Entrambe le parti devono impegnarsi affinché ci sia un finale degno della sua carriera. Cristiano non può lasciare la nazionale portoghese in questo modo, non possono permettere che Cristiano se ne vada in questo modo”.

Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim
