📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan put on a show for their fans at San Siro on Sunday evening as they beat Frosinone 5-1 to move back into the top four.

It was a game that promised entertainment from the early stages, and Milan took command thanks to an own-goal from Gabriele Calvani and a much-needed goal from Goncalo Ramos, before Patrizio Masini scored to halve the deficit.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri ran away with things in the second half, with Ardon Jashari and Alphadjo Cisse netting off the bench before Christian Pulisic got a goal of his own to add some gloss to the scoreline. There were chances to make it an even bigger margin, but five would have to do.

Given that Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus had all won prior to kick-off, it was important that Milan matched their results to keep up the pressure at the top end of the table, and they did so in emphatic fashion.

Sources indicate that ruben Amorim made just one change to the starting line-up from the side that won against Genoa before the break, with Alphadjo Cisse dropping out and Davide Bartesaghi coming in. It was uncertain from the line-up named what the system would be, as has often been the case with the Portuguese coach so far.

In a recent development, frosinone started the game better and called Mike Maignan into action inside the first minute with a close-range header that was saved, though the flag was up. Then, a deflected strike from Masini on the edge of the box ended up scraping the upright and going behind for a corner.

It has been revealed that however, it was Milan who struck first at San Siro. Luka Modric deserves the plaudits for an outstanding through ball to find Adrien Rabiot’s run in behind, and the Frenchman’s square pass was heading towards Christian Pulisic’s run but was turned into his own net by Calvani, leaving Palmisani rooted.

The frantic pace of the early stages continued, as a lovely exchange between Diego Moreira and Pulisic saw a threatening cross turned behind. A few minutes later, Yunus Musah found Moreira who had a shot deflected for a corner, which Goncalo Ramos rose and met well but headed over the bar.

It has been revealed that frosinone kept providing reminders that they too pose a threat going forward, such as on the quarter-hour mark when Kvernadze surged down the left and got off a low shot from a narrow angle that Maignan had to parry behind. The corner wasn’t properly dealt with, and Cittadini flashed one across the six-yard box that Rabiot had to put into the stands.

Recent findings suggest that just like with the first goal, Milan punished Frosinone for not making the most of their spell of pressure. Goncalo Ramos was the man who started and finished a flowing counter-attack, robbing Calvani of possession before running towards goal. Musah’s through ball was run onto by the electric Moreira, who found Rabiot, and the Frenchman’s cut-back was tucked away by the Portuguese.

It has been revealed that the two-goal lead was very quickly halved though, as Frosinone got the goal their pressure had threatened. Kvernadze’s run down the left and cut-back from the byline was scuffed onwards by Ghedjemis into the path of Masini, who toe-poked it in at the far post.

In the 34th minute, there was a moment that enraged the Milan players, staff and fans. The referee blew his whistle for a shirt pull on Rabiot just as Milan went through on goal with two men in behind and just the goalkeeper to beat. The official apologised, but it felt like a certain goal had been taken away.

It has been revealed that it was a half played at a hundred miles an hour, and it ended that way too. Pulisic flashed an effort over the bar from a good position, while Davide Bartesaghi’s low cross towards Ramos was cut out in the nick of time as Milan continued to get joy down the flanks.

Recent findings suggest that amorim opted to make an intriguing change at half-time, bringing off Bartesaghi and replacing him with Ardon Jashari. This change in turn saw Musah shift to left-back, a role that he played against Genoa in the last match, and from minute one.

The change proved to be an absolute masterstroke, as Jashari scored inside three minutes. A ball was sent long to Ramos who knocked it down to Rabiot, whose first touch was a lovely through ball to the Swiss midfield. It looked like he had overrun it with the square option not used, but he lashed a shot in at the near post.

Not long after the goal, Ramos gestured towards the bench that he felt some discomfort. He wanted to play through it but Amorim took no risks, opting to bring Alphadjo Cisse on to lead the line.

According to recent reports, there was a rather rare occurrence in the 54th minute, as Milan were awarded an indirect free-kick after Palmisani picked up a back pass from Calvani. Modric laid it off to Rabiot, but the goalkeeper made up for his error with a good save.

Continuing the trend of impact substitutions, Cisse got his ninth goal of the season right on the hour mark. A Frosinone corner was cleared and Pulisic found Moreira who had the Italian for manufacturer, and he finished the through ball by the Belgian past Palmisani with his trademark composure. The offside flag went up, but after a long check the goal was given.

Milan continued to look like scoring every time they got out of their own half, and Pulisic joined the fun in the 68th minute with a goal of his own. Frosinone again left one man back for a corner that was cleared, allowing the American to easily outpace Terzic with a run from inside his own half, dinking over Palmisani to make it 5-1.

Industry observers note that with 20 minutes left on the clock, Amorim brought Strahinja Pavlovic and Pervis Estupinan on for Diawara and Musah. The final change saw Omari Hutchinson replace Pulisic.

According to recent reports, pavlovic looked far from 100% when he came on, appearing dizzy at certain moments. The head coach seemed to suggest coming off so as not to risk things, but he played on.

Industry observers note that milan had chances to make the scoreline even more impressive, with Moreira and Hutchinson squandering a couple of chances on the break. However, at full-time the team were rightly applauded by the San Siro crowd.

McInnes believes Cup final incentive will fuel Rangers in vital run of fixtures

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (902 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.
  • Published: 10:52 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:13 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Rangers boss Derek McInnes insists the incentive of next month's Premier Sports Cup Final can fuel his players as they prepare to embark on a vital run of fixtures.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 10:52 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:13 EST, 23 November 2026.

Rangers boss Derek McInnes insists the incentive of next month's Premier Sports Cup Final can fuel his players as they prepare to embark on a vital run of fixtures.

A 2-1 triumph over Motherwell on Saturday night stretched Rangers' unbeaten run to 13 matches after Ryan Naderi struck a late winner at Fir Park.

McInnes' side will host a revitalised Aberdeen at Ibrox on Tuesday night, before two further home matches against Falkirk and Dundee United over the next week.

They will then face a double-header against Hibs, with a league clash at Easter Road swiftly followed by the cup final.

McInnes insists no player is guaranteed their place in the team - and challenged them to earn their place for the Hampden showpiece as they look to win the first trophy of the season.

'I think the squad looks strong at the minute,' said the Ibrox boss. 'We've got good options and good options from the bench to turn to.

Derek McInnes has led Rangers on a 13-game unbeaten run in all competitions.

'In this little run of fixtures, hopefully everybody will start to play a wee bit more of their part and hopefully more winning performances.

'I don't think I'll mention it [the cup final] too often, but they are not daft, they see that and everybody wants to play in the team.

'Anybody who's in the team needs to keep playing well to stay in the team and anybody who's not in the team needs to train right and take advantage of their minutes.

Recent findings suggest that 'We make that point often enough. Sometimes you've got to go away to tough venues like Motherwell and do the hard work and get the reward.

'But there's bigger games, more games like cup finals to take part in, so everybody wants to play in that one.

'I'm sure it does us no harm. I think it keeps the fans bubbling along, a chance of silverware, so when it comes along hopefully, as I say, we're in good form.'.

Rangers are on a strong run of form and haven't lost a game since they were dumped out of Europe against Jablonec at the end of August.

The victory over Motherwell maintained their position in second in the table, four points adrift of Celtic with a game in hand.

Up against an Aberdeen side buoyed by their first win under upcoming boss Mario Frick at the weekend, McInnes wants his players to keep the pedal to the metal.

'I think it's unusual with five games now away from Ibrox, four in the league and the cup game, and now the fixtures kind of run the other way,' noted the Rangers boss.

'We've got some good fixtures at home but I think we always look at little blocks in the weeks, and where we're looking to try and get to by a certain period, and get certain points and certain targets.

'But first thing's first now with Aberdeen. We've got to make sure we're a strong home team again. Hopefully we can score a few more goals but, ultimately, as long as we win the game, I'll be happy.

'I think there's always a wee concern when you've got so many away on an international break, but obviously now with the January break gone, this is us working right through to March.

'When you look at those little blocks of games, and where the teams are, it's important that we just put our shoulder to the wheel.

'Every game is going to bring up different challenges and just because we're at Ibrox, it's an advantage, but it doesn't guarantee anything. We've got to use that advantage properly.

'As I say, we've got some fixtures now ahead of the cup final. Hopefully we can get into the cup final in good form and with some strong performances.'.

Venezuelan striker Kevin Kelsy could be in line to start against Aberdeen.

Kevin Kelsy could be in line for a bigger role this week after fatigue caused by his return from international duty limited his involvement in Saturday's win over Motherwell.

The Venezuela striker was only fit enough for a substitute appearance after enduring a gruelling journey back from a friendly in Russia, with Derek McInnes admitting the travel disruption had taken its toll.

'When you go away on international duty, they go to some far-flung places and playing a friendly in Russia is not the best preparation,' said the Rangers boss.

'There was a point on Thursday morning when we were really worried about whether he was getting back. To have ten-and-a-half hours in an airport all day Thursday isn't ideal preparation.

In a recent development, 'He was gubbed on Friday. He was very tired when he spoke to me and told me he hadn't really slept.

According to recent reports, 'It's been a bit unusual, the preparation. We sent him home early on Friday to get a good sleep and look after himself, but we just made the call we thought was the right thing to do.

'We needed everybody at it on Saturday and we've got a substantial week ahead of us where he can play his part, hopefully from the start in one or two of these games.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lotito e Fabiani sono stati vicini al tecnico nel fine settimana, senza affrontare con lui il discorso mercato.

It has been revealed that il mercato della Lazio sarà bloccato: crediti ed escamotage non sono bastati a ripristinare il saldo zero. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, Lotito e Fabiani conoscono la cifra necessaria per rimuovere lo stop, al di là del giudizio della Commissione di controllo. Nel frattempo, la squadra di Gattuso ha chiuso per la prima volta le prime dodici giornate senza sconfitte.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Nel 1972/73 la prima sconfitta arrivò contro il Milan, per 3-1, in una gara dell’undicesimo turno recuperata dopo la quattordicesima giornata. La serie positiva raggiunse così tredici partite, ma non si trattò di dodici giornate iniziali completate senza perdere.

Il confronto richiama tre stagioni e altrettanti piazzamenti: lo scudetto nel 1973/74, il secondo posto nel 2022/23 e il terzo nel 1972/73.

A Formello prevale comunque la prudenza. Anche la Lazio allenata da Baroni, due anni fa, aveva iniziato con numeri non troppo lontani da quelli attuali, pur giocando le Coppe. Per questo Gattuso e la squadra fissano quota 40 come primo traguardo, senza alzare le aspettative.

Nel fine settimana Lotito e Fabiani sono stati vicini all’allenatore, ma non hanno affrontato con lui il tema del mercato.

Gattuso valuta anche un ingresso a gara in corso del capitano, dopo le partite saltate con Napoli e Lecce.

Recent findings suggest that mattia Zaccagni si allena full time e può giocare sabato a Torino. Secondo quanto riportato da Corriere dello Sport, Gattuso deve decidere se schierarlo dall’inizio o utilizzarlo a gara in corso. La valutazione passa dai test del capitano e dalle condizioni di Noslin, risparmiato nell’ultimo allenamento.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Restano due allenamenti prima della trasferta. Zaccagni continuerà a essere valutato, mentre si attende il rientro di Noslin. Con entrambi pronti, Gattuso potrebbe riproporre il tridente formato da Isaksen, Noslin e dal capitano. Se invece Zaccagni partisse dalla panchina, Pinamonti giocherebbe da prima punta per la terza volta consecutiva.

Nella decisione pesano anche le partite successive, contro l’Atalanta e nel derby. Zaccagni si era fermato contro il Cagliari e ha saltato Napoli e Lecce. Ha ancora pochi allenamenti nelle gambe: Gattuso e lo staff misurano gli sforzi anche attraverso i risultati dei test, senza voler correre rischi.

According to recent reports, se non partirà dall’inizio a Torino, l’ipotesi è un ingresso a gara in corso per riprendere ritmo, seguito dalla partenza dal primo minuto contro l’Atalanta. Il percorso è pensato anche in vista del derby.

Senza Zaccagni e Tavares, la Lazio ha utilizzato maggiormente la destra per costruire gli attacchi. Contro il Lecce, da quella parte sono arrivati l’assist di Isaksen per Noslin e il cross di Floriani per Taylor, che ha poi servito l’olandese per il secondo gol.

Recent findings suggest that con Tavares e Zaccagni disponibili, la corsia di riferimento è invece la sinistra. Lì la squadra sviluppa scambi e triangolazioni tra Tavares, Taylor e il capitano; Nuno può anche accentrarsi. Sulla destra Floriani resta spesso più bloccato, Frattesi attacca lo spazio e Isaksen cerca la conclusione più del cross.

It has been revealed that sono due modi diversi di avanzare. Il lavoro di Gattuso punta a mettere la squadra nelle condizioni di costruire e attaccare attraverso entrambe le corsie, in base agli uomini disponibili.

L’ex portiere spiega anche perché non frequenta i social e quale momento degli allenamenti gli manca.

Industry observers note that secondo quanto riportato da La Repubblica, Angelo Peruzzi ha smesso di fare il dirigente della Lazio perché non si divertiva più. Lo racconta in un’intervista a La Repubblica: «Sono stato dirigente della Lazio, poi ho smesso: non mi divertivo più.».

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

According to recent reports, peruzzi oggi vive lontano dalle apparizioni televisive. «Vivo a Blera, il mio paese in provincia di Viterbo, mi piace la campagna e stare tranquillo. Non mi annoio, le giornate volano, la vita vola», dice parlando delle sue giornate.

Recent findings suggest that alla domanda sul perché il calcio non gli piaccia più, Peruzzi risponde: «Non sputo nel piatto dove ho mangiato per tanto tempo, però mi domando cosa sia rimasto dentro quel piatto. Passione, a occhio poca».

Il discorso si sposta sul rapporto tra calciatori e pubblico. Peruzzi ricorda che, quando giocava, non amava concedere interviste: riteneva impossibile dire la verità senza avere problemi e pensava che questo portasse a risposte banali o a essere considerati stupidi. Poi parla dei social, assenti ai suoi tempi: «Quando giocavo, non amavo le interviste perché dire la verità era impossibile, troppe grane. E allora si diventa banali o si passa per stupidi. E non esistevano i social, questi strumenti spaventosi che hanno stravolto le nostre vite. Io non li frequento: perché mai dovrei raccontare a tutti cosa ho mangiato a colazione?».

Il workshop intende ribadire quanto già illustrato nel primo tavolo, tenutosi lo scorso 6 ottobre: il diabete non rappresenta alcun limite nel poter fare sport,.

Si terrà oggi alle 18 il secondo seminario del ciclo ‘Diabete in Libertà – Sport e Diabete’, fortemente voluto dalla Fondazione Lazio ETS, avente come focus il rapporto tra sport e diabete. L’incontro, realizzato in collaborazione con ANIAD, l’Associazione Nazionale Italiana Atleti Diabetici e AMD, Associazione Medici Diabetologi, si svolgerà con due modalità: in presenza nella Torretta di Piazza della Libertà e anche on line tramite zoom.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Sources indicate that il numero 1 al mondo del tennis, ha avuto la sua prima diagnosi di diabete nel 2001, a soli 4 anni. Il campione tedesco ha reso nota la sua condizione nel 2022.A illustrare ai partecipanti tutte le possibilità che la scienza e la medicina mettono a disposizione dei soggetti affetti da diabete, sarà il professor Felice Strollo, specialista in Endocrinologia e docente di Medicina Aeronautica e Spaziale. Strollo attualmente ricopre anche il ruolo di Membro del Comitato Scientifico dell'ANIADIl seminario odierno è rivolto a tutti i pazienti, agli addetti ai lavori e non solo a sportivi professionisti. L’obiettivo è chiaro: far comprendere che con il diabete si può convivere serenamente, fare sport e condurre una vita senza alcun tipo di condizionamento.

In a recent development, il seminario avrà luogo oggi alle 18 presso la Torretta di Piazza della Libertà. Per favorire la massima partecipazione, sarà possibile accedere anche tramite Zoom. L’ID riunione è 896 06 29 3452, il codice d’accesso è 929913.

Scotland's World Cup prize must not become a missed opportunity

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (583 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:23 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EST, 23 November 2026.
  • Confirmation that Scotland will co-host the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup is an undoubted boost for the game in this country.
  • Staging a global showpiece with England, Wales and Northern Ireland is indeed a potential game-changer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 15:23 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 15:36 EST, 23 November 2026.

Confirmation that Scotland will co-host the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup is an undoubted boost for the game in this country.

Staging a global showpiece with England, Wales and Northern Ireland is indeed a potential game-changer.

The joint bid projected that the competition would attract 3.5billion viewers worldwide. And that 4.5m tickets would be sold across the host nations.

But the key for Scotland will be the impact it has on girls taking up the sport, supporters watching it and professionals playing it north of the Border.

Scotland captain Caroline Weir has already described it as a ‘pivotal’ moment, a ‘real opportunity’ to drive momentum and reach another level, domestically and internationally.

Sources indicate that she’s right. It is an opportunity, of the once-in-a-lifetime variety, but a word of caution is in order. Opportunities are not enough in themselves to be transformative.

They have to be embraced, exploited and squeezed for all they are worth so that every last drop of their potential is properly fulfilled.

Star player Caroline Weir believes co-hosting the World Cup could be pivotal for women's football in Scotland.

It would be criminal if the powers-that-be got complacent about this priceless gift and made assumptions about its long-term legacy.

More players, more fans and more media coverage would be hugely exciting, but it will all be wasted if not supported by facilities, coaches and the safeguarding that goes with it.

Recent findings suggest that it has happened before. Interest in athletics rocketed after Glasgow 2014, but a poor infrastructure, which continued to rely on volunteers, prevented a grassroots boom.

And how many times have we heard Judy Murray complain that Scottish tennis squandered the opportunity presented to it by her son, Andy?

Scotland’s women played at the World Cup in 2019. Their game has grown since then, but the national side have not been to another major tournament and the domestic product is still a shadow of its English counterpart.

Sources indicate that only a handful of Scottish teams have full-time players. The wages are way behind those on offer down south. And professional men’s clubs could do much, much more to develop the sport. It’s no wonder the Scottish league can’t keep its better players.

The opposite is true in England, where the success of the national team is often attributed to the level of investment by the FA and the backing of sponsors across the country.

The good news is that Scotland have made a start on that front with something called Project 2035, which aims to transform girls' and women’s football over the next decade.

The Scottish government has stumped up an initial £250,000 to help with the 10-year plan, which outlined a number of key objectives earlier this month.

In a recent development, they want to grow participation at grassroots level, increase the number of women working in football - as coaches, leaders and decision-makers - and quadruple the number of fans. The hope also is that Scotland will progress beyond the group stage of at least one World Cup by 2035.

According to recent reports, having those ambitions is one thing; making good on them is quite another. The government, the league, clubs and the ruling body: all should be thrilled by this opportunity but they should also feel the pressure that it brings. For it is their responsibility, their duty, to make the most of it.

Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions

📅 22 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (4981 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur.
  • Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.
  • But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

According to recent reports, sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

“He is a top player, no doubt about it,” said head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

Industry observers note that “He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”.

A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the new season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh.

Later in the first half, Sangaré won a free-kick in his own half thanks to some quick feet and the action produced a massive cheer from the home fans.

Tonali was the subject of chants of “what a waste of money” from Brentford supporters. It was a volley that sailed high over the crossbar that prompted that particular song, but Tonali was not just off target with his shooting.

He lost possession on a couple of occasions at both ends of the pitch and allowed Brentford players to glide past him during the opening stages of the match. He struggled to get around the pitch and Tottenham generally lacked desire and fight – two things that clubs cannot buy.

Recent findings suggest that richarlison, Lucas Bergvall and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky can all be disappointed with Brentford’s second goal. Richarlison’s hold-up play was terrible, Bergvall produced a weak challenge that allowed Mathias Jensen to take the ball and shoot, and Kinsky parried the ball straight into the path of Vitaly Janelt, who scored.

Kinsky has been trusted to take over from Guglielmo Vicario as Tottenham’s number one this season, but this was not a good start.

Recent findings suggest that vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ.

De Zerbi spent much of the first half telling his back four to get higher up the pitch and it was perhaps understandable that captain for the day Archie Gray, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson looked like a group of strangers.

This was the foursome’s first competitive game together, but De Zerbi will need his Tottenham players to get to know each other as fast as possible if they are to challenge for Europe this season or even finish in the top half of the table.

Industry observers note that bergvall and Conor Gallagher were hooked at half-time, with Tottenham two goals behind and De Zerbi clearly unimpressed. But the Italian’s changes did not prompt an instant response. In fact, things got even worse.

Once again, Sangaré was heavily involved. He produced a well-hit shot that Kinsky had to save. For the second time, the goalkeeper failed to push the ball out of trouble and Michael Kayode was able to score.

Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU.

Igor Thiago missed a penalty after substitute Rodrigo Bentancur fouled Kevin Schade, as Spurs threatened to completely collapse with the result already pretty much decided.

Igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h.

Industry observers note that de Zerbi can console himself with the fact his Spurs team will quickly look a lot different. There are more fresh faces to come in, with winger Savinho on the brink of joining and Tottenham hoping Omar Marmoush will follow him from Manchester City.

Mikey Moore, who forced Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher into two second-half saves, is expected to join Cologne on loan and Mohammed Kudus is close to returning from injury, while Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro will come back in.

But if ever there was proof that spending a fortune offers no guarantee of happiness, then this was it.

Roberto De Zerbi has admitted that major-spending Tottenham Hotspur “are not a team yet” after watching his newly introduced-look side fall to an opening-day defeat to Brentford.

Tottenham have splashed out over £200m on new players, but head coach De Zerbi has warned it will be impossible to set any targets until they become a team.

Record £100m signing Sandro Tonali made his competitive debut for Tottenham, along with fellow latest signings Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson.

Tottenham have been tipped to challenge for European qualification, having finished 17th in each of the last two seasons, but De Zerbi acknowledged those optimistic predictions may have come too soon.

In a recent development, his team looked like strangers in their humiliating loss at Brentford and the Italian mentioned: “We are not a team yet for a lot of reasons. We can fix the target [for the season] when you become a team. Before you become a team, you can’t say what you can do.

Recent findings suggest that “You can’t become a team from the transfer market on paper. You become a team when the players find a connection, a spirit, a soul.

According to recent reports, “We are not at the right point in our physical condition for a lot of reasons. Late from the World Cup and because in Australia [on pre-season], we don’t work in the right way. But no excuses, it’s a normal situation when you are building a new project. I don’t want time but we have to pass through these problems.

It has been revealed that “I am surprised by the result and performance. They [Brentford] deserved to win and we played very bad. I knew we were not in the right condition. We can’t find an excuse. I am sorry for the result and performance.

It has been revealed that “Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke and Sandro Tonali are not in the best physical condition. We knew that before the game. We have to improve on that and many other things, like organisation and pressing.

“We can improve promptly but first, we have to understand this game better. I know their physical condition and [they are] fresh players but we have to put something more.

Industry observers note that “We had to fight more. Players know I have a lot of confidence in them and we hope to improve promptly. Until we reach these conditions we have to suffer and today is an notable defeat. Maybe we can wake up stronger.”.

We had some problems with the timing of the pressure, we arrived too often late. We lost too many duels to compete with Brentford. I am sorry for that and sorry for the defeat. We have to improve in the physical condition and the organisation.

It was the first game and part of our journey, we knew we had a lot of new players. To become a team I noted before the game we need two things, soul and style of play. We didn’t fight in the right way. Brentford is maybe one of the most important teams in the Premier League in terms of duels.

It was a game, especially in the first half, in one direction. We were not in the right position to make the high pressure, with Mikey Moore on the left centre.

According to recent reports, we didn’t play well, we didn’t play in the right way. I think not because we don’t remember last season, because these players are good people but we lost too many duels. One of the best qualities of Brentford is the one-to-one, the man-to-man and the set-pieces.

In a recent development, really pleased. Felt like there was a performance coming, you never really know after pre-season. The reality is the first game of the season comes and it can quickly come unstuck. I felt good for a number of weeks about how we were coming together. I was pretty pleased.

According to recent reports, our fans were amazing today. There is a genuine connection here that helps. I thought we started the game brilliantly and they were fully engaged. We want to be relentless. We looked like a real team.

That’s what we wanted, we wanted to start sharp, we want to show people what we’re made of and we did that today. We know last season we were one point off, this year, we’ve added quality people to the squad.

He’s been unbelievable, I can’t praise him high enough. He’s one of them players that we might lose the ball you just know he is going to win it back and he gets us on the counter-attack so quickly.

Is that Pedro Porro, Micky Van de Ven and Mohammed Kudus could be back for the next game against Newcastle, and Savinho ought to be through the door.

According to Opta, Brentford won the xG battle 3.96 to 0.47, taking 26 shots to Spurs’s nine. De Zerbi’s team finished the game with 59 per cent possession, but that is inflated by Brentford sitting off when three up. It’s the most xG Spurs have conceded in a single game since a 6-3 defeat by Liverpool in December 2024.

Less Christ the Redeemer more Christ, that was terrible.

"I think that sums it up"Fair to say this Spurs fan wasn't pleased with their performance 😅 pic.twitter.com/ZAdVaVbjlS.

Possibly Brentford’s best performance under Keith Andrews, though that may be overstating the strength of the opposition. This was a complete display: they pressed Spurs, they played through Spurs, they played over Spurs, they dominated Spurs from set-pieces and their defenders bullied Spurs’s forwards. It will be interesting to hear from De Zerbi and whether he is philosophical or irate. This is far from Spurs’s ideal projected team, but still unacceptable.

It has been revealed that kinsky palms away a Damsgaard corner, and Yarmoliuk slices his shot over the bar. We are deep into stoppage time, and Brentford’s players are still pressing Bentnacur and Senesi and making them play with their heads down.

According to recent reports, just four minutes of added time to play but Spurs have more defending to do in the shape over another Brentford corner. They survive, but Brentford quickly establish possession again.

It would appear Lord Sugar is still watching:.

To all Spurs fans don't worry this is all tactical to lure other teams into believing we are a easy touch. #coys.

Sources indicate that another Brentford debut: Callum Wilson replaces Igor Thiago. Destiny Udogie has replaced Archie Gray for Spurs. “You should have signed for a big club!” sing the Brentford fans, in reference to the club almost signing Gray two summers ago. Football fans never forget.

Recent findings suggest that another Brentford goal would put them top of the table, for what that is worth. Spurs enjoying some possession in the Brentford half now, but it is entirely sterile.

Industry observers note that igor Thiago’s shot is blocked, Brentford still look the more likely team to score the next goal. Jadon Anthony indicates he has a long throw, which might be a small reason why Brentford decided to sign him. Janelt then drags back Maddison.

Jadon Anthony involved in some Brenford pressure that results in a long throw and a corner, but the fresh man then slices a volley over the bar. Standing ovation at the Gtech for Sangare as he makes way for Damsgaard, while Hickey replaces Kayode. Be tough to beat his performance as debut of the weekend.

Industry observers note that michael Oliver letting some meaty challenges go, the game is quite feisty despite the scoreline. Schade launched himself into a tackle on Solanke but he did not really catch him with his studs.

A few Spurs fans may have thought better of staying to watch the final 20 minutes. I wonder “if” this Spurs fan has switched the television off?

In a recent development, first match if season . Smiling before the game. Hope to be smiling after. pic.twitter.com/hsTc79PBti.

According to recent reports, richarlison beats the turf and Ajer punches the air after the Brentford defender wins the foul. Andrews is making another couple of changes: Jensen and Ouattara off, Yarmoliuk and fresh signing Jadon Anthony on.

Two more Spurs changes too: Maddison and Solanke on, Moore and Richarlison off.

Really sharp save from Kelleher to keep out Moore’s powerful shot from close range. Moore has at least carried a threat for Spurs in the second half, but they are struggling to sustain much pressure.

Tonali with a hit from 25 yards but it deflects comfortably into the arms of Kelleher. Surely a (Kew?) bridge too far for Spurs to dig out any kind of result from here.

De Zerbi looks a little resigned on the touchline, he will know that this is far from his ideal Spurs team on the pitch but that cannot excuse such poor standards.

Sources indicate that he fails to open his account for the season. Sent Kinsky the wrong way, but he dragged the penalty just a touch and it cannoned off the post. The lead remains three.

It has been revealed that igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h.

Spurs are being overpowered here, they cannot cope whenever Brentford come forward. There were appeals for handball against Van Hecke after Janelt swivelled and shot, but the foul is given against Bentancur for bundling over Schade. A complete mess for Spurs.

Any hope that the half-time double change would bring a revival now appear forlorn.

But here is a chance for Mikey Moore! Robertson forward to good effect, and his low cross arrives to Moore at the back post but his shot was too close to Kelleher. Almost crept through his legs.

Well that is surely game over. Cracking strike from Sangare from the edge of the box after a Brentford corner is cleared, they have always been so good at winning those second balls. Driven strike, good save from Kinsky and Kayode is first to the rebound to score from a couple of yards.

Michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU.

Recent findings suggest that vital defensive header from Van Hecke to repel Sangare’s dangerous cross, and we enjoy our first look at a Kayode long throw. Some Strictly Come Dancing moves from Senesi and Collins in the penalty area, and the referee has a word with them. It continues when the throw is taken, and Sensi has a chunk of his shirt, but VAR notes the Spurs man was fouled beforehand.

Will we see a different Tottenham in the second half.

Gallagher and Bergvall hooked, replaced by Bentancur and Fernandes who makes his Spurs debut.

According to recent reports, 15 - There was 15 passes in the build-up to Keane Lewis-Potter's opening goal for Brentford, only Michael Kayode's goal v Wolves in March (19) and Rico Henry's goal v Bournemouth in December (18) have seen more in a Premier League goal for the Bees under Keith Andrews.Busy. pic.twitter.com/8j5RZWFxvH.

Recent findings suggest that this has been a dreadful start to the season by Tottenham. Sandro Tonali has barely looked like a £10m player, let alone a £100m midfielder and, maybe unsurprisingly, De Zerbi’s players look like strangers. He will demand a major improvement in the second half. Keith Andrews will be delighted - maybe other than the fact the game isn’t already dead. His team have been dominant.

Brentford utterly dominant, there has been an alarming gulf in industry, precision and class between the two teams. Spurs will surely improve, both in the second half and as the season goes on, but this has fallen well below the standards you expect of a team with European aspirations. If a few of these players never played for De Zerbi again they could have no complaints.

No sign of a Spurs revival at half time, Brentford playing through their press with ease and then have space to run into. Kayode wins his header at the back post but no player was there for the knockdown.

Recent findings suggest that crucial block from Ajer after Spurs’s best piece of combination play around the box, before Tonali slashes a volley well over the bar from distance. Cue “what a waste of money” from the home fans.

Richarlison has been non-existent up front for Spurs, bullied by Collins and Ajer.

Tonali with a stray midfield pass to Outtara which rather sums up the Spurs performance so far. Surely there will be sweeping changes from De Zerbi at half time. Solanke, Maddison and Fernandes are the three players you’d have in mind.

“You’re going down with the Fulham,” is the chant from the Brentford fans.

Sources indicate that lewis-Potter swings in a dangerous cross, headed down by Kayode, and Van Hecke stoops to block Outtara’s shot. The whistle goes for a high boot.

It has been revealed that this is far from Spurs’s strongest hypothetical team but they are being taken to the cleaners here. Spurs caught in that Brentford man-to-man press again and the ball bounces off Richarlison. Jensen shoots with power from the edge of the box, and Kinsky bats the shot back into danger, and there was Janelt to poke the rebound home. Brentford in total control.

In a recent development, vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ.

Spurs’s defence breached again, and Outtara really should have made it two but his first touch was far too heavy and Kinsky was able to clear. Spurs will not be the only team to struggle against this Brentford front three. Schade won the flick on, Thiago swept the ball across the box, but the finish was lacking from Outtara.

Outtara fouls his former Bournemouth team-mate in the Spurs box. A lovely chipped pass forward from Schade releases Thiago in the left channel and another spell of home pressure begins. Lewis-Potter roaming everywhere. Then Brentford win a free-kick which will go in the mixer. Senesi fouled Outtara.

Industry observers note that bergvall floats in a decent cross from the left but it splits Richarlison and Moore. Sweden manager Graham Potter is in the stands watching Bergvall. Van Hecke is known for his progressive passes, but he overhits one through for a Brentford goal kick.

Recent findings suggest that spurs players not happy with Michael Oliver. Conor Gallagher feels he was pulled back in midfield, before Oliver blows for a 50:50 in Brentford’s favour.

All so simple for Brentford to get at Spurs again, and it takes some excellent defending on the cover from Robertson to deny Outarra who could have been through for a second goal.

Industry observers note that igor Thiago’s header hits the bar but the flag goes up for offside. Brentford’s man-to-man press is smothering Spurs at the moment, they cannot break through it to establish any territory higher up the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that igor Thiago makes enough of a nuisance of himself to force Senesi to put the ball out for a throw, Brazil vs Argentina in the match up. Brentford just look sharper and more match-ready all over the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that half a chance for Spurs to reply with a quickfire equaliser, but Tel’s free-kick was tame and deflected through to Kelleher. De Zerbi can have no complaints, it was one-way traffic before the goal.

Well that’s a good early impression from Sangare. He played a lovely one-two before picking out Lewis-Potter for Brentford’s goal.

To say this opening Brentford goal was on the cards would be a mammoth understatement. The home team are finding it so easy to progress the ball to dangerous positions around the Spurs box.

In a recent development, the upcoming man Sangare is involved, playing a one-two at the edge of the area, before picking out Lewis-Potter who was unmarked on the penalty spot. Brentford’s left back popping up in the box, and it is a simple finish.

Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the newly introduced season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh.

Industry observers note that pretty much Spurs’s first meaningful foray over the halfway line, but Gallagher’s shot from distance is wild. In other news, Jon Bon Jovi is in the stands. He popped up at a few games at the World Cup.

Brentford continue to make inroads down their left, Lewis-Potter driving at Gray and whipping in a dangerous cross that glanced off Van Hecke at the near post and only just wide of the far post. The corner is swung to the unmarked Sangare at the back post, and his header loops well over.

Industry observers note that brentford continue to look the better team, moving the ball at pace in the final third, but Schade stumbles up against Bergvall in the box. Spurs yet to settle of establish any possession in the game so far.

Recent findings suggest that collins then catches Gallagher on the foot, as the Spurs man rushed into a challenge to close the defender down. Not much in it.

From that free-kick, Jenson’s delivery was a wicked one: inswinging and flat to the near post, and the ball glanced off Robertson’s head and behind for a corner.

Jensen then tees up Lewis-Potter for an ambitious volley from the edge of the box, and there are hopeful appeals for a handball penalty against Gallagher, and then Collins fails to divert to follow up cross on target.

Spurs under some pressure early on.

Not the most distinctive contrast between the two kits, but not as bad as Newcastle vs Bayer Leverkusen in pre-season.

Brentford on the front foot in the early exchanges, Sangare involve in their first attack, but Tel runs back to defend well against Kayode.

Schade then wins a free-kick from Van Hecke in a crossing position wide left, the forward’s feet were too quick for the Dutch defender.

The usual rendition of Hey Jude before the game in south west London.

[On three of the back four being newly introduced signings] I have a significant confidence because all three are very notable players with experience and qualities. They have been working for one month and we have no problem with them.

[On Gray wearing the armband] He’s very young but he is a significant personality. great behaviour and he deserves to be a captain today. He cannot suffer too much pressure because he is an crucial player for us for a long time.

[On if there is more business to be done] We have not the right or complete squad today but no excuse we have the qualities to compete against an crucial team with a clear style, they are very strong in set-pieces and long balls especially.

This will be a first look at latest signing Mamadou Sangare for Brentford fans. Lots of people have tipped him to be one of the signings of the summer. I haven’t seen enough of him to give an opinion but it will be interesting to see how he gets on against Tottenham’s first-ever £100m man Sandro Tonali.

There’s a decent chance this Tottenham starting line-up will not play again together for the rest of this season. Mikey Moore is expected to move to Cologne on loan, while Savinho’s arrival will relegate Mathys Tel to the bench. Spurs also have Mohamed Kudus and Xavi Simons to return from injury. De Zerbi will want a good start to the season, but this is not the Tottenham side he will be relying upon moving forwards.

It has been revealed that there will be no easing into life at Spurs for Robertson, who faces Dango Outtara in one of the game’s key duels. The Scot has plenty of experience of course, but there were signs towards the end of time at Liverpool that he had started to struggle in one-on-ones against wingers.

Sources indicate that archie Gray will become Tottenham’s youngest-ever captain tonight. Aged 20 years and 163 days, he will beat Steve Perryman’s record of 20 years and 260 days. On Friday, De Zerbi listed all of his captains with Gray down in fifth place. Fresh permanent captain Micky van de Ven misses the trip to Brentford through injury.

If we include the league goals Mikey Moore scored while on loan at Rangers last season, Spurs’s front three scored 22 league goals combined last season. By contrast, Igor Thiago, Kevin Schade and Dango Outtara scored 37 between them in the Premier League. Brentford are firm favourites with the bookies for this one, and that difference in firepower is probably why. Omar Marmoush could help matters.

Seventeen-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett is one of the outstanding players in the country at his age group, and there is a lot of excitement about him at Spurs. Post-Kane, the club’s academy has not delivered much bona fide first-team quality, but Williams-Barnett appears on that trajectory.

Brentford XI: Kelleher, Schade, Jensen, Thiago, Ouattara, Sangare, Ajer, Collins, Lewis-Potter, Janelt, Kayode.

Subs: Valdimarsson, Hickey, Henry, Pinnock, Yarmoliuk, Wilson, Anthony, Damsgaard, Schuster.

Your Bees to kick-off the 26/27 season 🐝 pic.twitter.com/nJO5emjgQM.

Spurs XI: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Senesi, Robertson; Gallagher, Tonali, Bergvall; Moore, Richarlison, Tel.

Subs: Dubravka, Danso, Maddison, Udogie, Fernandes, Solanke, Bentancur, Davies, Williams-Barnett.

Our Spurs side on the opening day 🤍🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/Uh5z221aTc.

Starting the season in west London 📌 pic.twitter.com/uglTu9zDvA.

Former managers Mauricio Pochettino, José Mourinho, Antonio Conte and Ange Postecoglou will all be scratching their heads about Spurs’ change of strategy in the club’s first post-Levy summer.

It was Postecoglou who publicly shared his belief that Spurs would never spend £100m on a player and yet, just over a year after his departure, the club splashed out exactly that on midfielder Tonali.

Whereas Postecoglou and his predecessors often had to answer questions over Spurs’ perceived profligacy, De Zerbi has been able to tease fans with promises of “bomba” signings.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Brentford vs Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League, a London derby between the smart spenders and the big spenders.

Recent findings suggest that that is probably an unfair dichotomy, because Spurs’s squad has been crying out for investment, and that has certainly arrived this summer. The club’s new leadership team has overseen more than £300m worth of purchases.

The arrival of Jean Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi, two of the league’s best progressive passers from centre-back, makes it clear that improving Spurs’s build up play is a priority for Roberto De Zerbi.

De Zerbi wants his teams to draw pressure from opponents and progress down the middle of the pitch with short passes, so it was imperative that Spurs upgraded in midfield. They have done just that by buying Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, for a combined £185m.

Industry observers note that spurs’s forward options remain much the same though, which could prove a drag in the season’s early weeks. Compared to Manchester United, Chelsea, and Liverpool, Spurs do not have the same firepower, but they should have more control and solidity this season.

It has been revealed that brentford lost just three league games at home last season, and they were unfortunate not to qualify for Europe. A lighter workload offers Keith Andrews the chance to consolidate on an excellent first season as head coach, and perhaps overtake some of those clubs with continental commitments.

Midfielder Mamadou Sangaré, signed for £39m from Lens, looks the pick of their summer business, tipped to be a £100m sale to one of the major boys (which is an unromantic perspective on the transfer, but very much Brentford’s model).

Asked about the Mali international, Andrews said: “He’s a very talented midfielder who can do lots of different aspects of that role.

“He’s a very focused, very determined and very ambitious young man. He’s very humble but equally as hungry to achieve impressive things. He’s certainly a player on an upward trajectory.”.

Forwards Jadon Anthony and Callum Wilson are other arrivals, and Michael Kayode’s long throws will continue to be a serious weapon.

Succede veramente di tutto a Banja Luka. L'Atalanta conquista tre punti importantissimi per la corsa al passaggio del turno in Conference League superando 3-2 il Borac con una rimonta al cardiopalma. La partita non era iniziata male ma tanti sono stati gli errori sotto porta della squadra di Maurizio Sarri. Come nelle migliori beffe ecco arrivare il vantaggio bosniaco di Juricic e da lì la luce si è spenta. Alla mezz'ora Detek firma il raddoppio e nella ripresa la musica non cambia con la Dea protagonista in negativo con tanti errori commessi in fase di finalizzazione.

It has been revealed that il finale però si accende. Al 74' viene espulso per fallo da ultimo Pascual che atterra Rowe lanciato a rete. All'86' Krstovic corregge in rete un cross al bacio di Bellanova e la partita si riapre. All'88' Herrera abbatte Zalewski e guadagna la via anticipata degli spogliatoi lasciando i suoi compagni in nove. Al 90' Kolasinac pareggia i conti e nel recupero, al 94', Zappacosta completa la rimonta con un diagonale vincente.

Al termine del match, l'allenatore Maurizio Sarri ha commentato a Sky Sport: "La verità è che abbiamo fatto una buona partita e abbiamo creato tantissime palle gol. Purtroppo in questo momento non abbiamo solidità difensiva e questa fragilità ci fa diventare tutte le partite più complicate. Però, se guardi i numeri della gara, le occasioni nostre ci sono: negli ultimi sette minuti abbiamo fatto tre gol su quattro palle abbastanza facili, mentre nei dieci minuti precedenti avevamo sbagliato tre reti da un metro".

Gerry Cardinale gave his thoughts after watching his AC Milan side run riot against Frosinone at San Siro this evening.

Sources indicate that it has been yet another few days where the Milan owner has made his presence felt. After landing in Italy, he was at Milanello and Casa Milan on Saturday for a series of vital meetings with the management and the squad, and then he watched first hand as the Rossoneri won tonight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

An own-goal from Gabriele Calvani got the scoring going, before Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all scored in the 5-1 rout of Frosinone. It could have been more in truth, but it was another display of the level this team can play at.

Cardinale was interviewed by Michael Cuomo of TeleLombardia after the final whistle having made his way down from the stands, and his comments were relayed by MilanNews.

According to recent reports, how happy is he? Is he satisfied?

“Well, I’m never satisfied, but the results speak for themselves. The boys were fantastic tonight. I hope you’re happy. I hope the fans are happy. I think the team is coming together really well.

“It’s a game, let’s keep it under control, but I’m really proud of the boys. This is a team. It’s a team that wants to win until the end.”.

Can you dream of winning the Scudetto?

Industry observers note that “Look, it’s November. We still have a long way to go. But we want to see improvements in every match. This weekend was very interesting if you look at the kind of results we’ve had. You can see that something is changing in Serie A.

“I was very happy to see us not just win, but win by that margin. And so, we have to build on that, but as Amorim says, every match is something to build on, and we have a long way to go. I personally still expect us to compete for the Scudetto, but it’s a long way off. One match at a time.

Sources indicate that “Now the focus is on the Europa League. Yes, and as Ruben said, we have to do both. European competitions are notable. Everything is a test. If you want to win a Scudetto, you have to do it all the way, and that’s what we’ll do.”.

Could signings arrive in January?

“Again: January is just another stage. As you know, the January transfer window is complicated. You have to be disciplined. You can’t just jump into something randomly. The only thing that will happen under my ownership is that every time we play in the transfer market, we’ll play to win.

Recent findings suggest that “That’s the theme. That’s the theme I said at the beginning of this year. So, if we make a move in any transfer window, January or June, it will be a move that will count.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Erling Haaland has unveiled a dramatic newly introduced look after cutting off his trademark blond locks.

The Manchester City striker revealed his latest buzzcut hairstyle on Sunday morning ahead of his side’s Premier League opener at home to Bournemouth later in the day.

Later in the episode, Haaland called a host of famous faces, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola, to get their opinions on his transformation.

Pep Guardiola's reaction to Erling Haaland's latest haircut. 😭😂📲 Watch: https://t.co/4KvxC9e5mx pic.twitter.com/QQBCKKpGkP.

Haaland, 26, has not sported short hair since his time at Borussia Dortmund, where he played three seasons before joining City in 2022.

Haaland removed his hairband during a 4-1 win over Arsenal in 2023 on a raucous night at the Etihad as City beat their title rivals to move one step closer to winning the league. There will be no need for one now, though, with a close-cut look to mark a newly introduced campaign.

It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a upcoming Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager noted. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

Industry observers note that “When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”.

Maresca added: “Hopefully we can do the things that we need to do. It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, this is for sure.

“But we need to adapt and we don’t want to keep players here that don’t want to stay.

“The normal thing in transfer windows is that you have to wait because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money.

Industry observers note that “It’s normal, I’m not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad there, for sure it will be different.”.

Published: 16:01 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 16:04 EST, 23 November 2026.

Manchester City legend Kevin De Bruyne insisted that any potential punishment for breaching financial rules will not change what Pep Guardiola’s team achieved and their memories of success.

The Belgian was a key pillar during the spell of unprecedented domestic dominance and has a statue commissioned outside the Etihad Stadium.

De Bruyne is back in town with Napoli for Tuesday’s Champions League tie, reiterating his ‘love’ for City and its owners, while revealing recent talks with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

The 35-year-old brushed off suggestions that silverware collected during his decade at City would be tarnished if the club lost their appeal and were sanctioned after being found guilty of the vast majority of charges levelled at them.

De Bruyne’s trophy haul – six Premier League titles, one Champions League, two FA Cups and five Carabao Cups – were largely secured outside of the nine-year period in which City were scrutinised, up to 2018.

‘I’m proud of what I've done as a football player,’ De Bruyne said. ‘Honestly, this is my club, I love the owners. I've talked about a lot of stuff outside football (with them), I've even spoken to Khaldoon about how to buy a club and everything.

The 36-year-old brushed off suggestions that silverware collected during his decade at City would be tarnished if the club lost their appeal.

Industry observers note that ‘It (stripping of titles) still doesn't change (anything), my football has not changed. I don't think a lot of people will change in their mind how they view me as a player, or how we played.

‘But everybody has his own opinion and other people may be disgraced a bit. I can't change anything about that.’.

De Bruyne’s final two seasons at City were plagued by injury before he joined Napoli on a free transfer in 2025 and his first return in last year’s Champions League lasted just 26 minutes as he hobbled off.

Classed as the greatest player in the club’s modern history, De Bruyne was typically forthright on the uncertainty surrounding his former employers after the guilty verdicts read by a three-person independent commission.

‘My feelings have never been different,’ he added. ‘Honestly, the way that I feel is just the way that I've been treated by this club, what I've done with this club for me personally, and how we've worked together as a group.

‘Of course, it's a lot of things that have been going on. I have nothing but affection for this club, and that will never change. Even now, the people who treated me and my family for 10 years is the most key thing.’.

De Bruyne left City under duress, vehemently disagreeing with the club’s decision not to offer him a new contract following a spate of injuries before choosing Napoli – and his long-term future in Serie A is now appearing in doubt.

Industry observers note that all eyes in Italy were on the midfielder’s public response to an interview published with his wife, Michele, in which she was reported to have criticised life in Naples and yearned for a move away. Those comments were taken out of context, according to a visibly frustrated De Bruyne, with PSV Eindhoven looking at securing a transfer in January.

De Bruyne left City under duress but revealed recent talks with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

But City supporters will have been more interested in how far De Bruyne went in backing their club ahead of next month’s appeal hearing.

‘In life there are rules, but everybody plays to the limit, I would say,’ he claimed, seemingly referring to how financial rules are interpreted by the Premier League’s elite clubs.

‘I played in between the white lines, and I competed with other players, and I had many experiences with my teams.

Sources indicate that ‘So for me that's the thing that I value most. The most crucial thing is the relationships between everybody that I had and how you manage these things, and I've given my all.’.

De Bruyne smirked as he discussed how he knew exactly how City would attack Napoli given his knowledge of the club and manager Enzo Maresca, who was Guardiola’s assistant during the 2023 Treble campaign.

Industry observers note that maresca is facing criticism after three defeats and a draw in their last four league games. The Italian called for calm over recent performances and believes that the transition from Guardiola was always going to represent a bumpy road.

‘It's like a reset, a restart, after 10 years with the same manager, same face, same words, same method,’ Maresca noted.

According to recent reports, ‘It's not easy to all of a sudden change. For me personally, it's all normal, and hopefully as soon as possible we can find the right balance in all the lines - defensive, midfield - and we can be consistent, which for me is the difference between us and other clubs.’.

Did you miss the feeling of scoring?

Il gruppo HBHC sostiene di aver tentato senza successo di estorcere denaro all’organizzazione calcistica.

Sources indicate that la Fifa ha confermato la sottrazione di dati interni durante un recente attacco informatico. Secondo quanto riportato da SportMediaset, Il gruppo di criminalità informatica Handsome Boy Hacking Club sostiene di aver prelevato oltre 12 GB di dati e di aver tentato, senza successo, di estorcere denaro all’organizzazione.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

La conferma è riportata dal sito specializzato in cybersecurity The Record, citato da SportMediaset. L’organizzazione calcistica, che ha sede in Svizzera, ha dichiarato che gli hacker hanno violato i suoi sistemi, ottenendo un «accesso non autorizzato a un insieme limitato di informazioni personali e aziendali».

Un portavoce ha affermato: «La Fifa sta collaborando strettamente con le autorità competenti, incluse le forze dell'ordine». La Fifa «condanna con la massima fermezza l'acquisizione e la pubblicazione illecite di informazioni, in particolare di dati personali. Tali azioni costituiscono una violazione grave e inaccettabile della privacy e possono avere conseguenze significative per le persone coinvolte».

Industry observers note that L’organizzazione non ha risposto a ulteriori domande sulla natura dell’incidente. La scorsa settimana, il gruppo Handsome Boy Hacking Club (HBHC) ha dichiarato di aver sottratto oltre 12 GB di dati alla Fifa. Il gruppo ha anche riferito di aver tentato senza successo di estorcerle denaro.

Tra le informazioni sottratte figurerebbero documenti d’identità e relativi all’immigrazione, documentazione finanziaria e legale, informazioni sulla governance e altri dati.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Doncaster Rovers will welcome Huddersfield Town to Club Doncaster Sports Village on Thursday for a Yorkshire Derby with importance at both ends of the League One table.
  • The visitors fell off the summit of the division following a defeat at the weekend, while their hosts drew on Saturday and only lead the relegation zone on goal difference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sam Varley | 25 Nov 2026 01:26.

Doncaster Rovers will welcome Huddersfield Town to Club Doncaster Sports Village on Thursday for a Yorkshire Derby with importance at both ends of the League One table.

The visitors fell off the summit of the division following a defeat at the weekend, while their hosts drew on Saturday and only lead the relegation zone on goal difference.

Doncaster Rovers head back into action on Thursday aiming to move clear of the relegation zone at the beginning of the League One weekend, having endured a difficult start to the campaign.

In their second season back in the third tier after promotion from League Two and a 14th-placed finish last time around, the Yorkshire outfit currently find themselves 20th having managed just 13 points from their first 14 outings, losing seven and winning just three of those.

Indeed, their last six outings have produced just four points, as Grant McCann's side broke up four defeats with a 2-0 home victory over Sheffield Wednesday, before falling to Luton Town and MK Dons away from home and experiencing mixed fortunes in a pair of cup ties against Rochdale and Kidderminster Harriers, losing to the latter in the FA Cup first round.

A trip to Yorkshire rivals Bradford City followed on Saturday, and the Rovers were at least able to bounce back from consecutive league defeats, twice falling behind and levelling through Jordan Thomas in the 78th minute and Sean Grehan deep into injury time to leave with a creditable point from a 2-2 draw.

Still only leading the bottom four on goal difference, Doncaster Rovers will now aim to bounce back to winning ways to put themselves three points above the drop zone before the rest of the weekend's action.

They face a tough test, though, as the visitors arrive in search of a rebound of their own to return to the top of the table.

Beginning their third straight season in League One and their first full one under the management of Martin Drury with the hopes of battling for promotion back to the second tier, Huddersfield Town have enjoyed a strong start as they headed into the November international break in top spot on 29 points from 14 games.

The Terriers won eight and only lost one of those while scoring 28 goals and conceding just 12, having headed into that break in a seven-game league unbeaten run in which they won four in a row before drawing against fellow promotion-chasers Luton Town in early November.

Then following a brief international break and a pair of cup outings against Exeter City and Liverpool Under-21s, Drury's side returned at home to Leicester City on Saturday but fell to just a second loss of the season in the third tier as Louis Page scored the only goal of the game for the visitors early in the second half.

That saw Huddersfield Town fall three points behind fresh leaders Stockport County, albeit with a game in hand, but only ahead of third-placed Oxford United having played a game more, and they will hope to quickly put things right and retake their place at the summit with a Yorkshire derby win on Thursday.

Doncaster Rovers League One form:.

Doncaster Rovers form (all competitions):.

Huddersfield Town League One form:.

Huddersfield Town form (all competitions):.

Doncaster Rovers remain without James Husband, Tommi O'Reilly and Francis Okoronkwo due to ongoing injuries, while Harry Clifton and Will Keane missed the game against Bradford and will likely remain sidelined too.

Brandon Hanlan led the line in that game and may continue to do so with Alfie May ineligible against his parent club, although James Collins is back in contention having made his Rovers league debut off the bench at the weekend following a long layoff.

Elsewhere, George Broadbent should again join Robbie Gotts and mainstay Owen Bailey in midfield.

Huddersfield Town are still without Murray Wallace, Jack Whatmough, David Kasumu, Herbie Kane and Marcus McGuane through injuries.

Drury should avoid making many changes despite the weekend's defeat, with Radinio Balker, Ibane Bowat and Sean Roughan having formed a strong back three in recent weeks and Cameron Humphreys and Archie Collins likely to continue their midfield partnership.

Joe Taylor and Derensili Sanches Fernandes have shone in attack, with the former scoring 10 goals in 14 league games and the latter notching up seven goals and six assists in 15.

Doncaster Rovers possible starting lineup:.

Simkin; Nixon, Grehan, Pearson, Senior; Broadbent, Gotts; Hutchinson, Bailey, Thomas; Hanlan.

Huddersfield Town possible starting lineup:.

Young; Bowat, Balker, Roughan; Bronkhorst, Collins, Humphreys, Mumba; Sanches Fernandes, Taylor, Radulovic.

Huddersfield Town will hope their rare defeat at the weekend does not derail their promotion push, and despite the hosts taking a point from Bradford at the weekend, we back the Terriers to bounce back on Thursday and outclass Doncaster.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In casa Napoli si lavora al mercato e la priorità è regalare ad Allegri un vice-Hojlund, un calciatore che possa dare ricambio in maniera consistente al danese e allo stesso tempo eventualmente giocare insieme.

Il club sembra intenzionato a puntare sull’attaccante campano Sebastiano Esposito, attualmente in prestito al Sassuolo, ma di proprietà del Cagliari. Il calciatore è il profilo adatto, per caratteristiche e cifre, per sostituire Lorenzo Lucca, sempre più ai margini e ormai giocatore che verrà ceduto a gennaio. La trattativa tra le parti è già cominciata e il Napoli sembra intenzionato a sferrare a gennaio l’attacco decisivo per Esposito.

Come riporta Il Mattino il Napoli è in pole per Sebastiano Esposito, nelle ultime settimane l’agente del giocatore Giuffredi ha incontrato Giovanni Manna e la trattativa è stata ormai già preimpostata. Il presidente azzurro De Laurentiis vuole riportare l’attaccante in Campania e il giocatore può arrivare a costi piuttosto contenuti per un profilo da Nazionale.

Il Sassuolo può riscattare Esposito per 10 milioni di euro circa e il Napoli potrebbe chiudere la trattativa a circa 14-15 milioni di euro, una trattativa che il Napoli potrebbe realizzare anche in prestito con obbligo di riscatto a fine anno. Le parti ragionano sul da farsi, ma sarà Esposito il nuovo attaccante per gennaio.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ruben Amorim insisted that he and his AC Milan team are not getting carried away despite hammering Frosinone, and are simply focusing on the next game.

Recent findings suggest that milan were in a rampant mood tonight at San Siro, as they put five goals past Massimiliano Alvini’s side and it could have been more in truth. Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic all scored, in addition to an own-goal that opened the scoring.

Sources indicate that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It has been revealed that it was important that the Rossoneri build on their victory over Genoa before the break, especially given that Lazio, Roma, Como and Juventus all won earlier in the round. In addition to that, several individuals shone and the team highlighted the levels that they are capable of.

Now, the challenge is to follow it up and get back on course in the Europa League in Greece on Thursday night. Amorim spoke to Sky after the final whistle to reflect on what was a very positive night for his side, with his words relayed by MilanNews.

Is that the best Milan performance since you have been here?

“It’s a good feeling, but it’s not just the result: it’s also about consistency throughout the 90 minutes of the match, but now we’re thinking about the next one. It’s always like that at this club, always thinking about the next one.

Industry observers note that “Tonight we played well, we were intelligent, courageous, and it highlighted towards the end of the match. We were tired, yet Frosinone continued to make transitions, but we managed to control them well.

Recent findings suggest that “We could have even scored more goals. Perhaps in the middle of the first half we struggled a little and we need to improve in one-on-one situations defensively, but anyway, it was a good night for us tonight.”.

Industry observers note that are you happy for Gonçalo Ramos? How is he?

“We can’t lose any more players. All our players can play every game, but we have little time to recover for the Europa League, so we can’t risk anything. It was better to take him off.

It has been revealed that “I imagine he wasn’t happy, but I’m still happy for him, for his goal, especially for the 2-0. It was a goal that made the difference in a match against a team that is very strong in one-on-one transitions.”.

Is Rabiot one of the best you’ve ever coached?

“I don’t want to say he could have had a better career because he played at PSG. Now he’s here at Milan and we want him to stay.

“Obviously, he’s a player who can play as a number 10, as an attacking midfielder, he can also play as a number 8, he can also play as a slightly deeper playmaker, even if he doesn’t like it.

“He’s definitely one of the best players I’ve ever coached, he’s one of the best midfielders in Europe right now.”.

What will you say ahead of Olympiacos?

Sources indicate that “The first thing I’ll say is that we have to win the match: if we don’t, then it will be really difficult to qualify for the next stage. Then I think that with Rabiot and Pulisic’s characteristics of playing between the lines, when they can’t play, we have to play and approach the game differently.

“But that’s not an excuse. I said the same things against Ferencváros: we should have played a different game and gotten a different result, but what I’m trying to say is that if we don’t win the match, it will be really difficult and things will go badly for us.

“Then, if we exit the Europa League, we’ll only play once a week and many players won’t play enough. However, I think that if we stay in Europe, we can play more and everyone will continue to grow.

Sources indicate that “Furthermore, if we don’t qualify, we will fail to achieve an key objective: so that’s why we have to start the match differently than Benfica and Ferencváros. We’ll see.”.

What can you tell us about Cisse as a striker?

Industry observers note that “I think he can play very well in that role, in that position. Tonight I chose Cissé to play in that position and not Camarda because against Frosinone, one-on-one, Cissé has these characteristics more. Tonight the goal wasn’t to keep possession, but to run and attack the space.

In a recent development, “Cissé is better at this than Camarda. We wanted to make more transitions than Frosinone, so it was a choice dictated by the player’s characteristics, but I think Cissé is good both as an attacking midfielder and as a central striker, and not just as a winger.”.
